research.abstract: Abstract Genome-wide association studies (GWAS) have identified numerous genetic variants associated with complex traits. However, linkage disequilibrium (LD) confounds these associations, leading to false positives where non-causal variants appear associated because they are correlated with nearby causal variants. This is particularly the case in highly polygenic traits where the genome can be saturated in causal variants. To address this issue, we propose LDeconv a method based on truncated singular value decomposition (SVD) that adjust GWAS summary statistics without requiring individual-level genotype data. This approach accounts for LD structure, isolates causal variants in high-LD regions, and improve the reliability of effect size estimates. We assessed the performance of LDeconv through simulations across various LD scenarios, conducted extensive sensitivity analyses, and applied the method to real GWAS data from the UK Biobank. Our results demonstrate that LDeconv effectively reduces false discoveries while preserving true associations, offering a robust framework for post-GWAS analyses, such as Mendelian Randomization.

research.abstract: Background: Individuals of African genetic ancestry are at high risk for heart failure (HF), which is often preceded by cardiac structural and functional abnormalities. Nevertheless, little is known about cardiac structure and function among Afro-Caribbeans residing in Tobago. This study aimed to investigate the epidemiology of cardiac structure and function among African Caribbeans in Tobago. Methods: A total of 924 participants (41-83 years) underwent clinical evaluation and transthoracic echocardiography. Images were analyzed for left ventricular (LV) mass index (MI), left atrial volume index, diastolic dysfunction (DD), LV ejection fraction (LVEF), global longitudinal strain (GLS), E/e' ratio, E/A ratio, and other echocardiographic measures. Cardiac structure and function were evaluated by age, sex, and HF stage. Results: The mean age was 61.7 years, with 61.4% women, 47.8% obesity, and 20.2% diabetes. Average systolic blood pressure was approximately 140 mmHg, and 76.7% had hypertension. Abnormal LV geometry was present in 77.1% of participants, predominantly concentric remodeling (69.5%). The prevalence of DD was 13.4%, LVEF <50% was 1.5%, and abnormal GLS ([≤]-18%) was 5.2%. Women had significantly higher E/e' ratios and a higher prevalence of Stage A and Stage B HF, whereas men had a higher prevalence of symptomatic (Stage C) HF. Participants aged 65-83 years had significantly higher E/e' ratio, concentric remodeling, and LV hypertrophy than those aged 41-57 years. Conclusions: Women and older adults have higher LV structural abnormalities and DD than men and younger adults. These results will be helpful to inform public health priorities related to cardiovascular health in Tobago.

research.abstract: Uropathogenic Escherichia coli (UPEC) presents a significant therapeutic challenge due to increasing multidrug resistance (MDR). While acquired resistance mechanisms are well-documented, the genetic variability of intrinsic efflux pumps like EmrD remains less characterized. This study investigated the genomic diversity and structural conservation of the EmrD transporter in ten clinical MDR isolates from the Kurdistan Region, Iraq. Isolates were screened for the emrD and β-lactamase genes, followed by emrD sequencing, phylogenetic analysis, and in silico protein modeling. Results confirmed the universal presence of emrD alongside multiple resistance genes. Phylogenetic analysis identified notable local genetic diversity, including a highly divergent lineage (DUH 11). Protein modeling mapped non-synonymous substitutions to transmembrane helices 6 and 12, regions critical for the "rocker-switch" conformational changes required for substrate translocation. These findings suggest that while EmrD is a stable component of the MDR machinery, localized genomic divergence may potentially influence efflux efficiency among clinical lineages, warranting future functional validation.

research.abstract: Tuberculosis (TB) remains the leading infectious killer worldwide. Brazil is among the 30 high-burden TB countries, however, genomic surveillance of Mycobacterium tuberculosis strains remains limited. We analyzed a convenience sample of 350 clinical isolates collected between 2016 and 2021 in metropolitan Rio de Janeiro to investigate genomic diversity, drug resistance and transmission dynamics. Among the isolates, 302 were phenotypically susceptible, while 48 showed resistance to at least one drug, including 35 multidrug-resistant (MDR) cases. Whole-genome sequencing predictions showed high concordance with phenotypic drug susceptibility testing (rifampicin 99%, isoniazid 99%, ethambutol 98%, streptomycin 97%). The most common resistance mutations were katG Ser315Thr and rpoB Ser450Leu. All isolates belonged to Lineage 4, predominantly sub-lineages 4.1 (Haarlem) and 4.3 (Latin American-Mediterranean). Despite incomplete sampling, genomic analysis identified 28 transmission clusters involving 23.2% of isolates, including a large MDR-TB cluster in the Tijuca neighborhood. Multi-year clusters indicated continued detection of closely related isolates over time, suggesting the persistence of related genomic lineages. No association was observed between resistance-associated mutations and treatment outcomes, although these analyses were likely underpowered to detect such associations. These findings highlight the need to strengthen genomic surveillance, molecular diagnostics, contact tracing, and treatment follow-up to control TB in the region.

research.abstract: Tuberculosis (TB) diagnosis remains challenging, particularly for extrapulmonary TB (EPTB), where invasive sampling, low bacillary burden, and limited sensitivity of nucleic acid-based tests in peripheral specimens hinder timely detection. Here, we report an immunology-driven strategy for biomarker discovery and development of a peptide-based serological assay targeting Mycobacterium tuberculosis zinc metalloprotease-1 (Zmp1). Based on the principle that antigenic regions containing overlapping B-cell and CD4⁺T-cell epitopes can promote strong antibody responses through linked recognition and cognate T-cell help, we used an immunoinformatics pipeline to identify two nested immunodominant Zmp1 peptide regions, Mtb-Zp-NT and Mtb-Zp-CT, enriched for overlapping B- and T-cell epitopes.Their diagnostic potential was evaluated using ELISA-based serological assays. A blinded pilot study (N = 137) demonstrated clear discrimination between active TB and TB-recovered individuals. An expanded validation cohort (N = 875), identified from screening approximately 6,086 individuals, included pulmonary TB (PTB), EPTB, TB-recovered individuals, household contacts, non-specific infection/inflammation, and healthy controls. Receiver operating characteristic analyses, supported by DeLong and bootstrap comparisons, demonstrated superior diagnostic performance of the peptide assays compared with Mtb-FL-Zmp1. Mtb-Zp-CT showed the highest accuracy (AUC = 0.93), with > 93% specificity and ~ 76% sensitivity.These findings establish immunologically optimized Zmp1 peptides as promising serological biomarkers for TB, including EPTB. Although further optimization may be required to meet WHO target product profiles, their high specificity supports potential use as an adjunctive diagnostic, particularly for EPTB, and as components of future multi-antigen panels. More broadly, this study demonstrates how mechanistically informed epitope selection can facilitate translation of pathogen-specific immune signatures into minimally invasive diagnostic platforms.

research.abstract: Abstract Sex-determining systems in flatfishes are highly diverse, and even closely related species can differ in both sex-determining loci and heterogametic systems. In common dab ( Limanda limanda ), the genetic basis of sex determination has not yet been established. Here, we investigated sex determination using pooled whole-genome sequencing combined with long-read genome sequencing of females and males from Iceland and Norway. Genome-wide allele-frequency analyses identified sex-associated regions consistent with male heterogamety (XX/XY), with the strongest signal on chromosome 16. Comparison of the existing reference assembly, which represents an X haplotype at this locus, with a haplotype-resolved male PacBio HiFi assembly revealed a ∼21.5 kb Y-specific insertion on chromosome 16. The insertion showed complete coverage in male pools but little or no coverage in female pools from either population. It contained a translocated genomic segment including a copy of gonadal soma-derived factor ( gsdf ) and a predicted gene of unknown function. Comparative genomic analyses were consistent with this segment originating from an autosomal gsdf -containing region on chromosome 1. Given the recurrent recruitment of gsdf as a sex-determining factor in teleosts, we designate the Y-linked copy gsdfY and identify it as the strongest candidate for the master sex-determining gene in common dab. Additional broad sex-associated differentiation on chromosome 19 was restricted to the Icelandic samples and may reflect population-specific expansion of the sex-linked region, although its structural basis remains unresolved. Together, these findings provide the first genomic characterization of sex determination in common dab and demonstrate how gene duplication and translocation can contribute to the evolution of novel sex-determining systems in flatfishes.

research.abstract: OBJECTIVES: To determine the proportion of resistance to five new and repurposed drugs (NRDs), identify risk factors for resistance, and characterize associated genetic mutations and transmission among people with multidrug-resistant or rifampicin-resistant TB (MDR/RR-TB) in Shenzhen, China. METHODS: Clinical isolates were collected from all people with MDR/RR-TB admitted to Shenzhen Third People's Hospital between January 2022 and December 2024. The minimum inhibitory concentrations of five NRDs - bedaquiline (BDQ), clofazimine (CFZ), delamanid (DLM), pretomanid (PMD) and linezolid (LZD) - were determined using the broth microdilution method. Risk factors for NRD resistance were identified using Firth's penalized logistic regression. Whole-genome sequencing (WGS) was performed on 99 isolates, including all NRD-resistant strains and randomly selected susceptible strains, to analyze resistance-conferring mutations, phylogeny, and clustering. RESULTS: Among 561 people with MDR/RR-TB, resistance proportions were BDQ 4.3%, CFZ 3.6%, DLM 1.1%, PMD 1.1% and LZD 1.4%. Prior NRD exposure (aOR=4.96; 95% CI, 1.95-12.61; P=0.001) and male gender (aOR=3.64; 95% CI, 1.15-11.56; P=0.028) showed strong positive associations with NRD resistance. BDQ exposure posed a higher risk of both BDQ- and CFZ-resistance than CFZ exposure. Based on the WHO mutation catalogue, WGS predicted NRD resistance with 100% specificity, sensitivity ranged from 16.7% to 75.0%. Notably, 37.5%-66.7% of resistant cases had no prior NRD exposure, and clustered isolates indicated transmitted resistance. CONCLUSION: NRD resistance among MDR/RR-TB patients in Shenzhen remains low. Although prior drug exposure is the primary risk factor, there is also evidence of transmitted resistance. NRD surveillance is essential to guide treatment and control transmission.

research.abstract: Introduction Abutilon fruticosum Guill. & Perr. is a drought-tolerant Malvaceae subshrub native to Saudi Arabia. However, no mitochondrial genome has previously been reported for the genus Abutilon . This study reports the first complete mitochondrial genome of A. fruticosum and evaluates its comparative and phylogenetic relationships within Malvaceae. Methods The mitochondrial genome was assembled, annotated, and analyzed for genome composition, repetitive sequences, codon usage, predicted RNA-editing sites, nucleotide diversity, synonymous and nonsynonymous substitution rates, collinearity, and phylogenetic relationships inferred from 32 shared mitochondrial protein-coding genes across ten taxa. Results The mitogenome was assembled as a circular molecule of 826,313 bp, with a GC content of 44.94%, and contained 37 protein-coding genes, 3 rRNA genes, and 21 tRNA genes. Comparative analyses of five Malvaceae mitogenomes revealed conserved codon-usage patterns, with weak-to-moderate bias influenced by nucleotide composition and functional constraints, but substantial variation in repeat abundance and distribution. DeepredMT predicted 397 RNA-editing sites in A. fruticosum , fewer than in Tilia amurensis , Gossypium trilobum , and Hibiscus cannabinus , but slightly more than in Adansonia perrieri . Simple sequence repeats and short dispersed repeats predominated, whereas G. trilobum had the greatest proportion of long repeats and H. cannabinus the highest repeat density. Nucleotide-diversity hotspots were detected in rpl16 , rps3 , cox2 , and rpl2 , while most protein-coding genes had dN/dS values below 1. The elevated dN/dS signal in rps4 suggested accelerated evolution or relaxed functional constraint, warranting further investigation. Maximum-likelihood analysis recovered A. fruticosum (tribe Malveae) as sister to the sampled Hibiscus – Gossypium clade with strong support. Discussion This study presents the first mitochondrial genome of Abutilon , expanding mitogenomic resources for Malvaceae. The A. fruticosum mitogenome shows conserved gene content and codon usage, alongside lineage-specific variation in repeat organization, predicted RNA-editing sites, nucleotide diversity, and localized sequence divergence. The phylogenetic placement is consistent with the accepted classification of A. fruticosum in Malvoideae and illustrates the potential of mitogenomic data for systematic studies within Malvaceae, although broader taxon sampling is needed to test this placement. This mitogenome provides a resource for marker development, population-genetic studies, comparative mitogenomics, and phylogenetic research on Abutilon and related Malvaceae lineages.

research.abstract: Abstract Accurate coding sequence prediction in short prokaryotic metagenomic sequences, such as Illumina reads, remains challenging due to sequence fragmentation, unknown sequence origins, and sequencing errors. Here we introduce DeepCDS, a deep learning-based ab initio coding sequence predictor trained on short prokaryotic sequences with and without simulated Illumina-like sequencing errors. DeepCDS integrates embeddings from the protein language model ESM-2 with nucleotide-level information to predict complete and partial coding sequences. Benchmarking on 215 phylogenetically diverse prokaryotic organisms demonstrates that DeepCDS consistently outperforms well-established and widely used methods in coding sequence detection across sequence lengths from 75 to 1,000 base pairs, including improved identification of both canonical and non-canonical start codons as well as stop codons, and greater robustness to different sequencing error profiles. DeepCDS also recovers more coding sequences from functionally uncharacterized genes and remains operational on sequences shorter than existing tools support. We additionally evaluate DeepCDS on a simulated metagenomic dataset from the Critical Assessment of Metagenome Interpretation initiative, where it likewise achieves the strongest performance among tested tools, and on a real human gut metagenome, where its predictions are more frequently supported by known proteins. These findings suggest that amino acid-level context, here provided by a protein language model, contributes complementary information for nucleotide-level coding sequence detection, especially at very short lengths. Ultimately, DeepCDS may help uncover the functional potential of the vast microbial diversity that remains genomically uncharacterized.

research.abstract: BACKGROUND: Tuberculosis caused by members of the Mycobacterium tuberculosis complex (MTBC) poses significant threats to animal health, public health, and wildlife conservation. Mycobacterium orygis, an emerging MTBC member, remains poorly characterized with respect to its epidemiology and transmission dynamics among Indian wildlife and livestock. METHODS: Fifty-five necropsy tissue samples from 21 captive wild animals were subjected to mycobacterial culture and a panel of molecular diagnostic assays, including multiplex PCR, Xpert-Ultra, and Truenat MTB/Rif. Confirmed MTBC isolates were characterized by drug susceptibility testing (GenoType MTBDRplus) and spoligotyping. Six isolates were selected for whole-genome sequencing (WGS), and phylogenetic analyses were performed against publicly available reference genomes. RESULTS: Of 55 samples, 38 were MTBC-positive and 6 yielded nontuberculous mycobacteria. Drug susceptibility profiling revealed 28 pan-susceptible isolates, nine with isoniazid monoresistance, and one with rifampicin monoresistance. Spoligotyping classified 10 isolates as CAS1-Delhi, 27 as orphan lineages, and one remained unassigned. WGS of six isolates, representing diverse host species and tissue types, identified four as M. tuberculosis (CAS1-Delhi lineage). Notably, one orphan isolate from a blackbuck was reclassified as M. orygis. Phylogenetic analysis revealed that this M. orygis strain was genetically distinct from other Indian wildlife strains and most closely related to a human-derived isolate from Karnataka, suggesting cross-host genomic relatedness. The remaining isolates clustered with Indian and global reference genomes; one was closely related to cattle-derived strains, whereas four were more closely related to human-derived strains. Low pairwise SNP distances (0-78 SNPs) with strong bootstrap support indicated close genomic relatedness across host species and geographic regions. CONCLUSION: This study shows the MTBC genomic diversity among various hosts. The phylogenetic relationships suggest that there is genetic relatedness among host populations such as M. orygis in a captive Indian blackbuck, which was in human contact for a long time. The study demonstrates the importance of integrated One Health genomic surveillance of mycobacterial infections at the human-animal interface and calls for more extensive, epidemiologically linked studies to look for cross-host transmission pathways.

research.abstract: Evaluating a 64-Species, 18-Locus Total-Evidence Supermatrix (L = 31,111 Aligned Columns; 11,436,768 Quartets), 48 Nuclear Functional CDS Orthologs, and 12 Single-Species Regional and Multi-Locus NCBI PopSet Cohorts (N = 432 Isolates) Exclusively via Constrained 100% Native Rust Bio-Suite Combinatorial Optimization (B = 1,000 UFBoot; 25,000 MCMC Generations) We reconstruct the Jurassic-to-Anthropocene global radiation, vector-host co-evolution, and historical demographic dynamics of Anopheles malaria mosquitoes across 544 verified NCBI sequence records comprising a 64-species, 18-locus supermatrix (L = 31,111 aligned columns), 48 nuclear functional coding sequences, and 12 single-species regional and multi-locus NCBI PopSet cohorts (12 × N = 36 = 432 isolates). Executed exclusively via constrained 100% Native Rust bio-suite optimization across 32 candidate RuNIE chains (total runtime 74.48 s; B = 1,000 UFBoot; 25,000 MCMC generations with 20% burn-in), RY3 purine/pyrimidine recoding under GTR+F+R4 reduces Dipteran AT-bias heterogeneity by 84.4% (RCFV = 0.0024 vs. 0.0154, ln L = -339,400.67), dating Crown Culicidae to 194.8 Ma, Crown Anophelinae to 108.4 Ma, the Gondwanan Nyssorhynchus–Cellia split to 78.9 Ma, and the African Gambiae Complex to 4.62 Ma. Native Rust quartet multispecies coalescent inference (runie-quartet-coalescent across 18 gene trees and 11,436,768 quartets in 46.97 ms) resolves 7,414,073 satisfied quartets (normalized Q = 0.6483, mean LPP = 0.8477) while ABBA-BABA tests confirm porous An. gambiae–coluzzii–arabiensis introgression (D = +0.4359 to +0.5177, Z = 12.11–13.06) and 61-state Goldman–Yang codon models identify strong purifying constraint on Orco/AgOR olfaction (ω₀ = 0.056) alongside diversifying selection on TEP1/LRIM1 immunity (ω₂ = 3.23), Anophelin/D7 saliva (ω₂ = 2.66), and VGSC/ACE1/GSTe2 resistance (ω₂ = 2.91). Finally, 12 coupled 25,000-generation Bayesian coalescent skylines reveal contrasting post-LGM savanna vs. Rift Valley expansions, Holocene agricultural/rice-paddy surges, an urban Horn of Africa An. stephensi invasion bottleneck, Amazonian BR-364 deforestation expansion, and an 89%–91% locus-specific effective population crash at the nuclear VGSC L1014F/C kdr selective-sweep locus under 21st-century pyrethroid bednet pressure while neutral mitochondrial (1Ne) and nuclear ITS2 (4Ne) demes remain demographic reservoirs. research.abstract: Wearable accelerometers enable continuous monitoring of physical activity (PA), yet conventional summary measures and population-wide clustering approaches may overlook disease-associated behavioral heterogeneity. Here we introduce LocPA, a computational framework that identifies disease-enriched PA patterns through confounder-adjusted activity profiling, similarity network construction, local disease-enrichment testing and community detection. Applying LocPA to 24-hour accelerometry profiles from the UK Biobank, we identified two recurring PA phenotypes across six diseases spanning cardiometabolic, neurological, psychiatric, renal and cardiovascular conditions: a low-activity phenotype characterized by reduced daytime activity and a sleep-disrupted phenotype characterized by reduced daytime and elevated nocturnal activity. In hypertension and diabetes, the sleep-disrupted phenotype was associated with greater disease burden and less favorable clinical and metabolic profiles, differences not consistently captured by conventional PA summary measures. LocPA also identified disease-specific temporal patterns, particularly in Parkinsons disease. Analyses in an independent National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey cohort supported the recurrence of hypertension- and diabetes-enriched patterns across populations and accelerometry measurements. LocPA provides a flexible, disease-driven approach for uncovering clinically relevant temporal PA patterns, with potential applications in disease risk characterization and personalized behavioral interventions.

research.abstract: Abstract Understanding how species diversity originates, accumulates and is sustained across heterogeneous regions is a core goal of macroevolutionary and conservation biology. The genus Huperzia is an ancient and cosmopolitan lineage of lycophytes, with species widely distributed in both temperate alpine and subtropical low‐ to mid‐elevation areas, offering ideal material for investigating the diversification history of early vascular plant lineages. Here, we utilized 87 plastid genomes from 23 species to reconstruct a robust phylogenetic framework within Huperzia and found that the development of the petiole and midrib should be considered supplementary diagnostic characters in future taxonomic revisions. Our spatiotemporal and spatial phylogenetic analyses indicated that temperate and montane regions, especially northeastern China and parts of the Qinghai–Tibet Plateau, preserve phylogenetically distinctive paleo‐lineages, whereas subtropical evergreen broad‐leaved forests contain younger lineages associated with ecological expansion and trait differentiation. This niche transition was accompanied by repeated leaf‐trait differentiation and shifts in plastid‐gene selection in subtropical lineages, with three positively selected genes ( rps19 , chlB and atpH ) identified by branch‐site analyses. This evolutionary strategy provides a new perspective for understanding how early vascular plants maintained a dynamic equilibrium between refugial conservatism and adaptive innovation.

research.abstract: Abstract Background Klebsiella pneumoniae is a common cause of neonatal sepsis in Africa, and is frequently hospital acquired. We recently reported an outbreak of multidrug-resistant K. pneumoniae sepsis amongst neonates at a rural hospital in The Gambia, West Africa, involving 57 cases and case fatality of 60%. Here we undertook a retrospective pathogen genomic epidemiology study of clinical and environmental K. pneumoniae isolated during the outbreak, to identify the outbreak strain, refine the epidemic curve, confirm the environmental sources of contamination, monitor control of the outbreak, and characterise the outbreak strain in the context of the local and global pathogen population. Methods and Findings We sequenced all blood culture isolates identified as K. pneumoniae from patients aged 0–59 months (n=51 available, 77% from neonates), together with K. pneumoniae cultured from environmental samples during the outbreak investigation (n=16), and 56 stored blood culture surveillance isolates available from the previous decade (34 from neonates). Sequencing was performed using Oxford Nanopore Technologies (ONT) Mk10 flowcells and a PromethION instrument, yielding mostly complete genomes (79%). Genomic analysis revealed 23% of isolates were K. quasipneumoniae and identified the outbreak strain as K. pneumoniae ST39 with capsular (K) locus KL62. This strain was responsible for 29 cases (16 fatalities) and was identified in three samples of intravenous fluids collected from the neonatal ward during the investigation. It harboured a ∼187 kbp IncF plasmid carrying the extended-spectrum beta-lactamase (ESBL) gene bla CTX-M-15 and aac (3)- IId , encoding resistance to third-generation cephalosporins and gentamicin, respectively. The outbreak strain was not identified amongst historical surveillance isolates, and it was distinct from a KL23-ST39 strain responsible for an earlier outbreak at the Sir Edward Francis Small Teaching Hospital in Banjul, the country’s capital 7 years prior. Comparing the outbreak strain with publicly available genome data for ST39 and its associated sublineage (SL) 39, we observed SL39 has diversified into three common clonal groups, each associated with multiple K types, that have spread across Africa, Asia and Europe and have been associated with outbreaks of neonatal sepsis in Africa and elsewhere. We find SL39 is typically multidrug resistant, however the specific ESBL and carbapenemase genes vary by geographic location. Conclusions Pathogen whole-genome sequencing refined our understanding of the outbreak, allowing more precise identification to refine case numbers and case fatality calculations, and for precise identification of multi-use intravenous fluid bags as the source of the outbreak despite other samples being culture-positive for unrelated K. pneumoniae . This highlights the importance of infection prevention and control in reducing neonatal fatalities in low-resource settings, and the critical risk associated with multi-use reagents and equipment when caring for vulnerable neonates. The genomic analysis enabled us to identify and characterise the outbreak strain at high resolution, and together with global data highlights SL39 as an emerging high-risk multidrug-resistant, globally distributed clone of K. pneumoniae, capable of sustained transmission and high fatality. Impact Statement Neonatal sepsis caused by Klebsiella pneumoniae kills an estimated 800,000 infants annually, with the greatest burden in sub-Saharan Africa where multidrug-resistant strains are increasingly prevalent. Yet genomic investigations of outbreak strains from rural African settings remain scarce, limiting our understanding of transmission dynamics and the global emergence of high-risk lineages. In this study, we apply whole-genome sequencing to a multidrug-resistant K. pneumoniae ST39 neonatal sepsis outbreak at a rural Gambian hospital, demonstrating how pathogen genomics can decisively refine outbreak investigations in low-resource settings: it corrected case counts, pinpointed contaminated multi-use intravenous fluid bags as the primary source, and revealed a novel ISKpn14-mediated chromosomal resistance island. Contextualising the outbreak strain within a global collection of 684 ST39 genomes, we identify sublineage 39 as a diversified, globally distributed, multidrug-resistant clone whose three dominant clonal groups have caused neonatal sepsis outbreaks across Africa, Asia, and Europe. Our findings reinforce the urgent need for sustained investment in genomic surveillance and infection prevention infrastructure in African neonatal units, and provide actionable data to guide targeted screening and vaccine design against prevalent African K. pneumoniae lineages. Data summary The raw sequencing data generated for this study have been deposited in the NCBI Sequence Read Archive (SRA) under BioProject accession PRJNA1367967. Individual isolate sequencing data are provided in Supplementary File 3 and are available under BioSample accessions SAMN53359187 through SAMN53359276, with corresponding SRA accessions SRR36200451 through SRR36200540. The complete genome assembly for a representative ST39 outbreak isolate, 38833B1 is available in GenBank under BioSample accession SAMN53359242, including the complete sequence of pNS39_A under GenBank accession PX620516 . Code used to generate the figures and reproduce the analyses presented in this study is available at https://github.com/efosternyarko/molecular-characterisation-klebsiella-pneumoniae-neonatal-sepsis-outbreak-gambia .

research.abstract: Tetrigidae is an early-branching family of Caelifera whose species live on damp ground, feed largely on mosses, algae and detritus, and often show wing and pronotum polymorphism. Which chemosensory and detoxification genes underlie this lifestyle is unknown. We generated an Oxford Nanopore PCR-cDNA transcriptome from a pooled sample of adult Hyboella guangxiensis (4.25 million full-length reads) and used it, together with protein homology, to filter the 17,996 machine-learning gene models of its chromosome-level genome to 15,338 supported genes without loss of BUSCO completeness. For nine families (OBP, CSP, IR, SNMP, P450, CCE, GST, UGT, ABC), full-length transcripts corrected 28 of 447 loci, including split and fused models, and brought protein lengths into agreement with orthologs of the sister species Bolivaritettix circocephalus (paired Wilcoxon p = 0.00066). Only 251 loci were supported by complete-ORF transcripts, and 101 had no full-length reads at all. Reconciliation of family phylogenies across eleven orthopteran genomes assigned 119 well-supported duplications to the Tetrigidae stem branch, dominated by P450 (42), UGT (27) and ABC (22) genes, and identified 63 homologous groups restricted to Tetrigidae. Five lineage-specific groups detected as transcripts in adults were validated at the genome level in four non-tetrigid outgroups: a CYP301A-like array, a Tetrigidae-specific UGT clade, two Tetrigidae-specific chemosensory proteins, a CYP9E2-like array and an esterase FE4-like array. Branch-site tests found episodic selection on some members of the UGT and CYP301A-like groups and in 7 of 28 recent paralog pairs, but not in the CYP9E2-like, FE4-like or CSP groups. These genes are candidates for the cuticular, chemosensory and dietary adaptations of pygmy grasshoppers to be tested with tissue-resolved data, whereas no family member could be linked to wing polymorphism.

research.abstract: Abstract Motivation Foundation models aim to learn useful representations of biological sequences, but are hindered by a lack of benchmarks to jointly evaluate predictive performance and variant attribution on diverse tasks. To this end, we present the Benchmark for Interpretable prediction from Genomes of Tuberculosis, BIG-TB. Results We curate over 17,000 genomes with high-quality sequencing data and experimentally measured antibiotic resistance phenotypes, combined with a curated list of WHO-catalogue of resistance-associated variants, and provide these data in an ML-ready format. BIG-TB defines two tasks: (1) predictive performance of antibiotic resistance phenotypes, and (2) attribution of predictions to known resistance-conferring variants. Using our tasks, we evaluate DNA- and protein-based foundation models, showing that DNA-based foundation models do not yet outperform simple machine learning baselines (mean test AUC = 0.888 vs. 0.865 for best CNN variant vs. best Evo2 variant across drugs). In a lineage-informed evaluation across DNA and protein modalities, predictive signal for well-characterized drugs was largely preserved (mean AUC 0.846–0.963). Across both evaluation settings, models with the highest predictive performance did not necessarily achieve the strongest recovery of resistance variants, underscoring the value of evaluating both predictive accuracy and biological interpretability. Overall, BIG-TB provides a reusable resource for developing sequence representations that are both accurate and mechanistically meaningful. Availability Code is available at SAGE-Lab-UMass/Big-TB-benchmark; data are available at figshare. Contact [email removed] Supplementary information Supplementary data are available at Bioinformatics online.

research.abstract: Abstract Human Satellite 1B (HSat1B) remains one of the least characterized classical human satellite DNAs, despite its massive abundance on the human Y chromosome. Its tripartite ∼2.5 kb monomer - comprising an AluY fragment, a GC-rich unit (here named H1B) and an AT-rich block - points to an evolutionary origin tightly linked to transposable elements (TEs). Here, we present the first comprehensive comparative genomic, phylogenetic, and transcriptional characterization of HSat1B across 10 primate species using Telomere-to-Telomere (T2T) and chromosome-scale long-read assemblies, combined with DNA-FISH, RNA-FISH and long-read transcriptomic analyses. We demonstrate that while canonical tandem HSat1B arrays are restricted to Homininae (human, chimpanzee, bonobo, and gorilla), the core H1B unit and its structural variants (H1Bsv1 and H1Bsv2) occur across all 10 primate genomes, including strepsirrhines (lemur). This indicates that the H1B sequence predates the assembly of the composite HSat1B monomer by at least 60 million years. H1B variants consistently map within TE-rich genomic contexts, supporting a stepwise, TE-mediated model of satellite diversification and mobilization. Within Homininae, humans exhibit a dramatic lineage-specific expansion driven by Yq12 amplification (∼14.2 Mb; 92% of total genomic content), whereas non-human great apes carry smaller, highly polymorphic autosomal and Y-linked arrays. Finally, we show that H1B-containing sequences are transcriptionally active in human and gorilla nuclei via RNA-FISH and characterize heterogeneous H1B/ Alu chimeric non-coding transcripts in the human male germline. Collectively, our findings uncover the birth and Homininae-specific expansion of a composite satellite DNA seeded by an ancient primate sequence module and sculpted by transposable elements.

items.title: Do divergent mitochondrial backgrounds alter the fate of nuclear alleles during hybridization and admixture?
items.summary: Hybridization brings together genetic variation from different populations or species into admixed genomes. research.abstract: Abstract Hybridization brings together genetic variation from different populations or species into admixed genomes. As selection sorts this variation, the fate of each allele is determined by its fitness effect in the new hybrid genomic background. Because mitochondrial genes coevolve with the nuclear genome, they may be especially sensitive to foreign nuclear backgrounds, making them potential “hot-spots” for hybrid incompatibilities. Here, we test whether selection against mitonuclear incompatibilities drives repeatable hybridization outcomes. Specifically, we experimentally evolved three sets of five populations of hybrid Drosophila melanogaster , each carrying the same nuclear chromosomes but paired with one of three increasingly divergent mitochondrial DNA backgrounds. We hypothesized that accumulated incompatibilities would result in different patterns of nuclear admixture among mitochondrial backgrounds. To test this, we tracked nuclear allele frequencies in all 15 populations by whole-genome sequencing at intermediate time points. After 25 generations, we observed that rapid genomic evolution produced a strikingly parallel mosaic of both nuclear ancestries, independent of mitochondrial background. Contrary to our hypothesis, we found no evidence that mitochondrial background shaped nuclear admixture, even for interspecific combinations. These results suggest that in species with large effective population sizes, efficient purifying selection limits the accumulation of mitonuclear incompatibilities, allowing selection on nuclear alleles to promote repeatable ancestry sorting immediately following hybridization.

research.abstract: Abstract Background Retinopathy and age-related macular degeneration (AMD) are the most common findings on fundus photographs of older adults, yet their frequency, correlates and visual consequences have been estimated in separate samples. We compared them in a national survey that graded both from the same images. Methods We analyzed 5593 adults aged ≥40 years in the US National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey 2005–2008 with photographs gradable for both conditions. We estimated survey-weighted prevalence, fitted identically specified logistic models for retinopathy (participants with diabetes) and AMD (full sample), and compared presenting visual impairment (better-eye acuity worse than 20/40) and self-rated vision across four groups: neither condition, retinopathy only, AMD only, and both. Results Retinopathy was more prevalent than AMD (9.54% [95% confidence interval (CI) 8.52–10.56] vs 6.52% [5.54–7.50]); AMD overtook it only from age 70 years. In participants with diabetes, retinopathy was associated with HbA1c (odds ratio [OR] 1.54 per percentage point; 1.33–1.78) and male sex (1.54; 1.10–2.17). AMD was associated with age (OR 1.09 per year; 1.07–1.11) and was less common in non-Hispanic Black adults (0.48; 0.33–0.71). Presenting impairment affected 4.91% of participants with neither condition, 7.09% with retinopathy only, 14.57% with AMD only and 26.15% with both. After age adjustment, impairment remained associated with AMD only (OR 2.23; 1.54–3.23) and both conditions (4.09; 2.28–7.37) but not retinopathy only (1.32; 0.91–1.90). Neither retinopathy nor diabetes was associated with AMD. Self-rated vision agreed poorly with measured impairment (κ = 0.15): only 12% of impaired participants rated their vision poor or very poor. Conclusions Retinopathy is the more frequent retinal finding in US adults aged ≥40 years, but AMD carries more of the measured visual impairment, independently of age. Grading diabetic screening photographs for AMD, and measuring acuity rather than asking about vision, would reach more people who see poorly.

research.abstract: Abstract Intraspecific variation in microbial symbioses is shaped by a variety of ecological and evolutionary processes. In geographically separated populations, divergence in genomic traits is expected due to dispersal barriers and habitat differentiation, whereas sympatric populations might exhibit functional convergence to the characteristics of a shared environment. While these two processes have been well documented in many animal and plant species, they remain understudied in symbiotic systems. Here, we examined these processes in Atlantic cold seep mussel species that associate with environmentally acquired methane and/or sulfur-oxidizing bacteria. Using genomic methods, we reveal an eco-geographical barrier between the Western Atlantic and Gulf of Mexico that influences the distribution of symbiont species and the level of divergence between holobiont populations. While host populations were only slightly differentiated across this divide, symbiont populations were structured both between and within regions. The sulfur-oxidizing symbionts contained different regional types of dissimilatory nitrate reductase, possibly due to variation in oxygen availability. The methane-oxidizing symbionts showed evidence for convergent evolution, such as retention of a secondary, iron-dependent methane monooxygenase in Western Atlantic populations, driven by local copper limitation. These findings advance our understanding of divergent and convergent adaptive mechanisms underlying intraspecific host-symbiont variation in horizontally transmitted symbioses. Lay Summary Mussels of the subfamily Bathymodiolinae are foundation fauna at deep-sea cold seeps, where they rely on methane- and sulfur-utilizing bacteria for nutrition. Little is known about how these symbioses have evolved across large geographic ranges and varying environmental conditions, although it is thought that mussels typically partner with symbionts whose traits are suited for the specific characteristics at their local habitat. In this study, we collected samples of three co-occurring cold-seep mussel species across thousands of kilometers in the Western Atlantic and Gulf of Mexico and used genomic methods to compare both the mussel hosts and their symbiotic bacteria. Within each species, we found that, while mussel populations did not vary much genetically across the two regions, the genomic traits of the symbiotic bacteria differed between locations. For example, different symbiont species in the Western Atlantic independently shared a comparatively rare enzyme for methane utilization, likely because of the specific environmental conditions at seeps in this region. This observation suggests the occurrence of parallel adaptations across symbiont species, underscoring the importance of environmental pressures in driving the evolution of microbial symbioses.

research.abstract: ABSTRACT Background Point-of-care ultrasound (POCUS) is a low-cost, radiation-free triage tool but lacks standardized acquisition protocols for tuberculosis (TB). We developed and evaluated a streamlined symmetric POCUS protocol for pulmonary TB in a high-burden setting. Methods Ugandan participants aged ≥13 years with confirmed pulmonary TB, household TB exposure, or a non-TB respiratory condition underwent an 18-position POCUS examination (12 lung zones and 6 pre-established extrapulmonary positions). Random Forest classifiers using prespecified pathologic features were developed in a fixed stratified 75/25 training/holdout split. All symmetric 2-, 4-, and 6-zone combinations were evaluated in training data. The best protocol of each size was locked and tested in the holdout set. Results Among 318 analyzed participants, 118 (37.1%) had pulmonary TB and 200 were TB-negative, including 102 with other respiratory conditions (ORC). The model-selected 6-zone protocol comprised bilateral anterior-superior, lateral-superior, and posterior-superior lung zones. For TB versus all TB-negative participants, the AUCs for the 6-zone, 12-zone, and 18-position protocols were 0.82 (95% CI, 0.73-0.92), 0.81 (0.70–0.92), and 0.81 (0.71–0.91), respectively (all P > 0.76). For TB versus ORC, AUCs were 0.81 (0.70–0.91), 0.85 (0.76–0.93), and 0.85 (0.76–0.94), respectively (all P > 0.45). The 2-zone protocol had a lower AUC than the 6-zone protocol for TB versus all TB-negative participants ( P = 0.004). Shred sign, consolidation, and B-lines with irregular pleura were the strongest TB-associated findings. Conclusions A fixed 6-zone lung POCUS examination showed similar discrimination for TB to more comprehensive 12-lung-zone and 18-position protocols. This supports a simpler, scalable approach to TB triage.

research.abstract: Abstract Atherosclerotic plaque vulnerability drives ischemic cardiovascular events, yet the cellular and molecular signatures distinguishing symptomatic from asymptomatic human plaques remain poorly defined. Here, we compared 53 symptomatic and asymptomatic human carotid plaques using single-nucleus (snRNA-seq; 17 samples, 19,100 nuclei; AtherOMICS biobank) and single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq; 36 samples, 68,983 cells; four public datasets), analysed independently and combined by meta-analysis. Across sequencing approaches, symptomatic plaques showed cell-state shifts toward later or terminal states in osteochondrogenic smooth muscle cells (SMCs) and CD4⁺ T cells, as well as transcriptional changes toward inflammatory and epithelial-to-mesenchymal transition (EMT) in endothelial cells (ECs), T cells, and fibroblasts. Nuclear profiling uncovered a depletion of fibroblasts in symptomatic plaques, marked by downregulation of RGS5 . Integrating these transcriptomic signatures with genome-wide association data for coronary, cerebrovascular, and peripheral atherosclerotic disease, we found that genetic risk was enriched primarily in vascular wall cells (SMCs, fibroblasts, ECs), rather than immune cell types. The analyses further nominated higher TWIST1 expression in ECs (colocalized with risk across four atherosclerotic phenotypes), lower GUCY1A1 expression in fibroblasts and macrophages, and higher MRAS expression in T cells as candidate driver mechanisms linking genetic risk to symptomatic plaque transition. These findings provide novel insights into cellular and molecular phenotypes associated with plaque vulnerability and identify potential driver mechanisms of symptomatic plaque transformation that could inform therapeutic development.

research.abstract: Abstract Objective To describe the role of hysterectomy in modifying the major atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease risk factors. Data sources PubMed, Cochrane Library, Embase, and ScienceDirect were searched from database inception to March 10, 2026. Study eligibility criteria Full-text randomized controlled trials, case-control studies, cross-sectional studies, cohort studies, case series, and experimental studies reporting new-onset cardiovascular events, diabetes mellitus, hypertension, dyslipidemia, or other metabolic effects following hysterectomy were eligible. Reviews and book chapters were excluded. Study appraisal and synthesis methods Study selection and data extraction were performed independently by multiple reviewers with conflicts resolved by consensus. Cohort study quality was assessed with the Newcastle-Ottawa Scale; a modified version assessed cross-sectional studies. Meta-analyses were performed using a generic inverse-variance random-effects model for each outcome, stratified by study design (cross-sectional versus cohort) and effect measure (adjusted odds ratio, adjusted hazard ratio, or relative risk). Narrative synthesis was performed for outcomes not meeting criteria for meta-analysis. Results Twenty studies (11 cohort, 8 cross-sectional, 1 mixed design) were included after screening 18,337 records from four databases. Hysterectomy was associated with significantly increased risk of hypertension (cross-sectional odds ratio 1.32, 95% confidence interval 1.18– 1.48; cohort hazard ratio 1.19, 95% confidence interval 1.09–1.30), diabetes (cross-sectional odds ratio 1.21, 95% confidence interval 1.11–1.32; cohort hazard ratio 1.20, 95% confidence interval 1.13–1.29), hyperlipidemia (hazard ratio 1.21, 95% confidence interval 1.13–1.29), obesity (odds ratio 1.24, 95% confidence interval 1.03–1.50), and metabolic syndrome (odds ratio 1.24, 95% confidence interval 1.08–1.44). Conclusions Hysterectomy is associated with increased risk of hypertension, diabetes, hyperlipidemia, obesity, and metabolic syndrome, key modifiable atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease risk factors. Active cardiovascular risk assessment and follow-up may be warranted for women who undergo hysterectomy, particularly at a young age.

research.abstract: Abstract Background Cultivated peanut ( Arachis hypogaea L.) is an allotetraploid crop (2n = 4x = 40) with an AABB genome that preserves extensive synteny between its two subgenomes. This characteristic, along with the availability of multiple genomic resources, provides a valuable framework for the comprehensive characterization of gene families and for inferring their evolutionary dynamics. Here we report a genome-wide analysis of the Dof transcription factor family in peanut (AhyDof), including phylogenetic inferences, gene structures, chromosomal locations, patterns of gene duplication, and expression analysis. Results ​A total of 66 non-redundant Dof genes (AhyDofs) were identified and unevenly distributed across the A and B subgenom​es. Comparative analyses revealed extensive conservation of gene structure, protein motifs, and chromosomal localization among homeologous genes inherited from the diploid progenitors, indicating that allopolyploidization contributed to family expansion while having a limited impact on gene diversification. Phylogenetic analyses placed AhyDofs within the four major angiosperm Dof lineages, supporting the evolutionary conservation of this family across flowering plants. Synteny analyses further identified chromosomal rearrangements and tandem duplication events contributing to the current composition of the AhyDof repertoire. Most notably, we discovered a novel group of six Dof genes associated with previously undescribed Pack-MULE transposons, designated AMuD, providing the first evidence of Pack-MULE-mediated transduplication in the genus Arachis . Structural and phylogenetic analyses suggested that these elements originated from non-autonomous MULEs and captured an ancestral Dof gene related to AhyDof-15.3. The dN/dS rate analysis suggested that transduplicated genes may have evolved under selective constraint, potentially indicating that functional constraints were maintained after mobilization. Comparative genomic analyses, PCR assays across diploid species, and Oxford Nanopore sequencing data suggested that AMuD elements originated within the B–F–K lineage of section Arachis and were maintained during peanut domestication and diversification. Promoter analyses revealed distinct cis-regulatory architectures among AMuD-derived genes, while transcriptomic data demonstrated their transcriptional activity, particularly in reproductive tissues. Conclusions The evolution of the peanut Dof repertoire in peanut was shaped by multiple mechanisms, including polyploidization, chromosomal rearrangements, tandem duplication, and lineage-specific Pack-MULE-mediated transduplication. The discovery of AMuD elements reveals a previously undescribed mechanism contributing to the diversification of regulatory genes in Arachis and provides new insights into the evolutionary dynamics of plant transcription factor families.

research.abstract: Abstract Fruit flavor and aroma are determined by the sugars-to-acid ratio and, most importantly, by the specific profile and abundance of volatile organic compounds (VOCs). While over 550 VOCs have been identified in strawberry fruit, fewer than 20 are believed to be key for aroma, with esters representing the predominant class. A major and stable quantitative trait locus (QTL) explaining up to 40% of the phenotypic variation in several medium-chain esters (MCE) was mapped at about 19 Mb in chromosome 6A, through both QTL mapping in a biparental population and a genome-wide association study (GWAS) in a diverse collection. Integration of transcriptomic analyses from bulks contrasting in MCE content and multiple tissues of ‘Camarosa’ identified the cinnamoyl-CoA reductase gene FaCCR1(6A) as the most likely candidate underlying this QTL. Subcellular localization experiments indicated that FaCCR1(6A) is localized at the cytosol, and its transient overexpression in fruits significantly increased MCE content, confirming its pivotal role shaping fruit aroma. Although CCR enzymes are known for their involvement in the biosynthesis of monolignols, molecular docking analyses supported the interaction of FaCCR1(6A) with aliphatic acyl-CoA substrates . In vitro enzymatic assays further demonstrated that FaCCR1(6A) can catalyze the conversion of aliphatic acyl-CoA substrates to the corresponding medium-chain aldehydes. These findings uncover a previously unrecognized function of FaCCR1(6A) in volatile biosynthesis while providing a mechanistic explanation for the phenotypic differences associated with differential FaCCR1(6A) expression. Furthermore, we have developed a predictive KASP assay to facilitate the selection of superior cultivars with enhanced fruit aroma in strawberry breeding programs.

research.abstract: Efficient evaluation of sequence data likelihoods and their high-dimensional gradients on phylogenetic trees improves inference under both maximum-likelihood and Bayesian frameworks. Here, we present BEAGLE 4.1, a high-performance library for statistical phylogenetics that incorporates new algorithms to evaluate these gradients on phylogenetic trees. We also provide new hardware implementations for both likelihoods and gradients supporting ARM NEON intrinsics and optimized matrix multiplication units -- called tensor cores -- on NVIDIA graphics processing units (GPUs). We benchmark the performance scaling of the library across a number of patterns and taxa on multi-core CPUs and GPUs, and compare the speedup afforded by NVIDIA and AMD GPUs as well as performance scaling with an increasing number of GPUs. We show that multi-core CPU implementations provide up to a fourfold speedup over single-threaded CPU implementations and up to an tenfold speedup for nucleotide and codon models, respectively, with performance generally improving as the number of taxa and site patterns increases. GPUs outperform multi-threaded CPU implementations for a realistic number of patterns, even for nucleotide models with a small state-space size of 4, while for codon models they provide substantially higher performance gains even for a single pattern or four taxa. Tensor cores on GPUs provide up to 2-fold speedup relative to standard CUDA cores for codon models. Using NEON instructions on ARM CPUs affords up to a $\sim 1.3$-fold speedup over non-SIMD implementation with the speedup going down to 1.1-fold at 8 CPU threads. We provide these new algorithms to evaluate the gradient and efficient hardware implementations for both likelihood and gradient calculations through BEAGLE 4.1, such that they can be readily integrated into phylogenetic software packages.

research.abstract: Abstract Understanding how gene flow shapes the distribution of genetic variation is essential for the conservation of rare and geographically restricted species. We investigated genomic structure, clonality, and mechanisms of gene flow in the federally endangered, serpentine endemic Dudleya abramsii ssp. setchellii (Jeps.) Moran using low-coverage whole-genome resequencing of 52 individuals representing 13 populations of D. a. ssp. setchellii , four populations of the geographically adjacent D. cymosa (Lem.) Britton & Rose, and two other subspecies of D. abramsii from San Luis Obispo County. Genome-wide comparisons were combined with analyses of clonality, isolation by distance, principal component analysis, phylogenetic reconstruction, pollinator observations, and a controlled seed dispersal experiment. Strong isolation by distance was detected both within a focal population and among populations across the species’ range, indicating that genetic differentiation increases predictably with geographic separation. Clonal reproduction was present, but restricted to individuals separated by only a few centimeters, contributing little to broader spatial genetic structure. Genomic analyses recovered D. a. ssp. setchellii as a distinct lineage exhibiting geographic subdivision within the species and identified a putative hybrid with D. cymosa . Field observations identified bumblebees as the dominant floral visitors, suggesting the potential for pollen-mediated gene flow, whereas a controlled seed dispersal experiment showed that most seeds traveled only a few meters under the artifically optimal experimental wind conditions. Together, these results suggest that limited seed dispersal may contribute to the pronounced spatial genetic structure observed in this serpentine endemic, although the relative contributions of pollen-mediated gene flow, geographic isolation, and genetic drift remain unresolved. These findings provide a genomic framework for conservation and identify geographically structured populations (east vs. west of Coyote Valley) as important units for long-term management.

research.abstract: Abstract BACKGROUND Active case finding (ACF) in India screens large populations to find few cases. AI-NETRA predicts neighbourhood-level tuberculosis (TB) risk from routine notification data and generates field microplans. OBJECTIVE To compare the yield and efficiency of AI-guided and standard ACF, and frontline acceptability. DESIGN Prospective quasi-experimental evaluation in four TB Units of Pune district, comparing two-week AI-guided sweeps (April to May 2026) with the routine campaign in the same units (December 2024 to January 2025). Primary endpoint: bacteriologically confirmed pulmonary TB per persons screened; secondary: all-forms yield, presumptive yield, referral precision, number needed to screen (NNS) and cost per case. Acceptability: 16 focus groups (n=100) and a survey of 101 ASHAs. RESULTS AI-guided teams screened 66,095 people and confirmed 10 pulmonary cases, against 9 among 177,322 in the standard campaign (rate ratio 2.98, 95% CI 1.09 to 8.29); NNS was 6,610 versus 19,702 and cost per case 66% lower. All-forms detection did not differ (15 versus 32; RR 1.26, 95% CI 0.63 to 2.39); the standard campaign had mobile X-ray. 96% of ASHAs reported finding the same presumptive cases while screening fewer people. CONCLUSION Geospatial targeting raised confirmed yield per person and lowered NNS; total detection did not differ. A concurrent, like-for-like trial is warranted.

research.abstract: 32-chain RuNIE phylogenomic and functional selection analysis across 64 species and 18 loci (L = 26,700 aligned columns; Lagomorpha outgroups, Sciuromorpha, Castorimorpha, Dipodoidea, invasive Muridae, and New World Cricetidae: Arvicolinae, Neotominae, and Sigmodontinae) coupled with 10,000-generation (20% burn-in) single-species Bayesian coalescent skyline reconstructions across three North American PopSets (Peromyscus maniculatus, Sigmodon hispidus, and Urocitellus parryii; 3 × N = 36 = 108 conspecific isolates) benchmarked against *MAFFT, *IQ-TREE/*LSD2, *PAML codeml, and *BEAST v1.10.4 The continental radiation of rodents (Order Rodentia) across North America via Paleogene Beringian corridors, Miocene grassland expansions, and Great American Biotic Interchange exchanges—coupled with the Anthropocene introduction of Old World commensal murids—established both the foundational small-mammal trophic guilds of Nearctic ecosystems and the primary sylvatic reservoirs for North America's major rodent-borne zoonoses. Here we execute a 32-chain RuNIE phylogenomic and functional selection analysis across an 18-locus, 64-species Glires supermatrix (L = 26,700 aligned columns with 7,979 parsimony-informative sites and 8,803 distinct site patterns) paired with independent 10,000-generation (20% burn-in) single-species Bayesian coalescent skyline reconstructions across three conspecific North American population datasets (3 × N = 36 = 108 isolates) benchmarking Native Rust against *MAFFT v7.526, *IQ-TREE v2.4.0 with *LSD2 v2.4.4, *PAML v4.10.10 codeml, and *BEAST v1.10.4. Our fossil-calibrated chronogram anchors the Glires root (Lagomorpha vs. Rodentia) at 65.2 Ma, Crown Rodentia at 56.8 Ma, the Sciuromorpha–Castorimorpha split at 36.4 Ma, Myodonta (Dipodoidea vs. Muroidea) at 46.5 Ma, the Muridae–Cricetidae divergence at 24.8 Ma, Crown Cricetidae at 18.6 Ma, and the New World Neotominae–Sigmodontinae split at 13.4 Ma. Codon selection modeling (*PAML codeml) reveals strong purifying constraint on the Sin Nombre hantavirus endothelial receptor ITGB3 beta-3 integrin (omega = 0.5319), intermediate selective constraint on the high-altitude and fossorial hypoxia axis EPAS1/HBB (omega = 0.0343) and rodenticide-detoxification locus VKORC1/CYP2C (omega = 0.2572), and diversifying positive selection on bacterial pattern-recognition receptors TLR2/TLR4 (omega = 0.2631) and the New World Arenavirus receptor TFRC transferrin receptor 1 apical domain (omega = 0.1453). Across the three single-species PopSet skyline cohorts, we resolve post-glacial forest/oak-mast expansion and contemporary ENSO Sin Nombre hantavirus / Lyme disease amplification in the North American deer mouse (Peromyscus maniculatus, N = 36, Ne = 433,194 to 653,847; *BEAST = 667,970), northward agricultural grassland expansion and Black Creek Canal / Tamiami viral irruptions in the hispid cotton rat (Sigmodon hispidus, N = 36, Ne = 1,534,254 to 1,753,302; *BEAST = 1,808,005), and post-LGM Beringian steppe-tundra recolonization and high-latitude permafrost-thaw dynamics in the Arctic ground squirrel (Urocitellus parryii, N = 36, Ne = 707,606 to 1,687,680; *BEAST = 1,740,336), while demonstrating that Native Rust achieves a 42.9-fold end-to-end speedup (13.88 s vs. 595.24 s Hybrid and 1861.52 s full External UFBoot). items.title: Ultra-low-dose same-target combinations control drug resistance across stages
items.summary: The emergence of drug resistance continues to limit the long term effectiveness of cancer therapies [1], as tumour cells adapt to therapeutic selective pressure through diverse genetic and non-genetic routes [2,3]. Despite advances in more potent and next generation inhibitors and mechanism based combination therapies [4,5], durable disease control remains difficult to achieve. Here we tested an…

research.abstract: The emergence of drug resistance continues to limit the long term effectiveness of cancer therapies [1], as tumour cells adapt to therapeutic selective pressure through diverse genetic and non-genetic routes [2,3]. Despite advances in more potent and next generation inhibitors and mechanism based combination therapies [4,5], durable disease control remains difficult to achieve. Here we tested an alternative strategy: combining multiple inhibitors directed against the same oncogenic driver, each at ultra low doses with minimal individual activity, to delay resistance emergence. In epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR) driven cancer models, such ultra low dose same target combinations (ULDCs) distributed individually weak perturbations across multiple inhibitors directed against the same target and achieved substantial growth inhibition in vitro and antitumour activity in vivo despite weak effects of the corresponding single agents. Under similar levels of growth inhibition (~50%), single-agent EGFR inhibitors generated resistant outgrowth, whereas a five drug ULDC delayed resistance emergence. Increasing the number of inhibitors further delayed resistance emergence, with no detectable resistant outgrowth observed for combinations containing 8 to 14 inhibitors within the experimental timeframe. The five drug ULDC also retained measurable growth inhibitory activity against gefitinib resistant PC-9/GR cells, and resistant cells arising under five drug ULDC treatment exhibited markedly greater reversibility following drug withdrawal than those arising under single agent treatment. Although pharmacological additivity or synergy may contribute to the collective growth inhibitory effects of ULDCs, the divergent long term resistance outcomes observed under similar levels of growth inhibition indicate that resistance behaviour is not determined by inhibitory strength alone. Instead, our findings support a model in which increasing same target inhibitor diversity progressively constrains the adaptive trajectories available during resistance evolution, while therapeutic perturbation architecture may also influence the stability of resistant states that emerge. More broadly, these findings support the concept of same target collective suppression, in which multiple individually weak perturbations directed against the same target can collectively produce substantial antitumour activity and constrain resistance evolution across multiple stages. We propose that increasing same target inhibitor diversity may restrict accessible adaptive trajectories, while therapeutic perturbation architecture may also influence the stability of resistant states.

items.title: Whole-genome analysis of drug resistance and transmission patterns in Mycobacterium tuberculosis from Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, Pakistan.
items.summary: UNLABELLED: The emergence of drug-resistant Mycobacterium tuberculosis strains presents a significant challenge to tuberculosis (TB) control programmes worldwide, particularly in high-burden countries, such as Pakistan. This study characterises the genomic diversity and drug resistance mutation profiles of M. tuberculosis isolates from Khyber Pakhtunkhwa using whole-genome sequencing (WGS). A…

research.abstract: UNLABELLED: The emergence of drug-resistant Mycobacterium tuberculosis strains presents a significant challenge to tuberculosis (TB) control programmes worldwide, particularly in high-burden countries, such as Pakistan. This study characterises the genomic diversity and drug resistance mutation profiles of M. tuberculosis isolates from Khyber Pakhtunkhwa using whole-genome sequencing (WGS). A total of 35 clinical M. tuberculosis isolates underwent WGS. Sequence data were quality-filtered and mapped to the H37Rv reference genome, characterising variants, including single-nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs). Lineage classification, drug resistance profiling, and identification of resistance mutations were performed using TB-Profiler software. SNP-based clustering was used to infer recent transmission events. All four major M. tuberculosis lineages (L1-L4) were detected; however, more than half of the isolates belonged to lineage L3 (CAS, n = 19; 54.3%). Almost all isolates were drug-resistant (34/35), including pre-extensively drug-resistant (pre-XDR, n = 15; 42.9%) and multidrug-resistant (MDR, n = 14; 40.0%) strains. The most frequent resistance-associated mutations included katG S315T (27/35) and inhA c.-777C > T (4/35) for isoniazid resistance, rpoB S450L (24/35) for rifampicin resistance, embB M306I/V (18/35) for ethambutol resistance, and gyrA D94G (8/35) and A90V (5/35) for fluoroquinolone resistance. Compensatory mutations were observed in rpoC and ahpC. Mutations associated with bedaquiline and clofazimine resistance (mmpR5 c.140dupA, c.138_139dupTG) were detected in single isolates. Interestingly, one isolate exhibited a deletion encompassing mmpR5, mmpL5, and mmpS5, potentially increasing bedaquiline susceptibility. Phylogenetic analysis using 6,635 genome-wide SNPs identified two transmission clusters with < 9 SNPs differences, suggesting ongoing local transmission. These results highlight the presence of drug-resistant M. tuberculosis strains in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, encompassing both globally recognised and novel resistance-associated mutations. Our findings underscore the critical need to integrate WGS into TB surveillance and control programmes in Pakistan to guide targeted interventions and curb the spread of resistant strains. SUPPLEMENTARY INFORMATION: The online version contains supplementary material available at https://doi.org/10.1038/s41598-026-62482-7.

research.journal: bioRxiv: the preprint server for biology
research.abstract: ABSTRACT Animal species differ dramatically in their overall size, yet the mechanisms underlying these differences are poorly understood. The Hippo pathway, first discovered in Drosophila , and widely conserved in mammals, regulates the nuclear levels of YAP1, a transcriptional co-activator that enhances the expression of growth-promoting genes. While experimental manipulations of this pathway elicit dramatic effects on tissue growth and organ size, it is not known whether, and to what extent, evolutionary divergence of this pathway has contributed to size differences across animals. Here we show that although YAP1 protein sequence is highly conserved between diverse mammals such as humans, elephants and blue whales, it diverges considerably among rodent species. While the human YAP1 protein is very similar to that of the largest rodent, the capybara Hydrochoerus hydrochaeris , those of smaller rodents such as the mouse Mus musculus and the vole Microtus oregoni show considerable divergence. An increased ratio of non-synonymous versus synonymous substitutions (dN/dS) in clades of small rodents compared to the background is indicative of relaxed constraint in these lineages, suggesting relative positive selection. When expressed in the developing Drosophila wing, capybara YAP1 was more potent at promoting growth than that of the mouse or vole. Following transfection into mammalian cells, capybara YAP1 is more effective at promoting expression of a reporter gene than either mouse or vole YAP1. Thus, by combining computational and experimental approaches, we show that evolutionarily divergent coding-region changes in YAP1 have likely contributed to the evolution of smaller body size in clades of rodents.

items.title: Two Axes of Sleep, One Heart: Dissociating Objective Sleep-Disordered Breathing From Subjective Sleep Duration in Cardiac Risk
items.summary: Background: Cardiovascular epidemiology has long treated "sleep" as a single exposure, although it denotes both an objective physiological state and a subjective behaviour. We tested whether these domains carry separable information about cardiac risk. Methods and Results: We derived an objective axis from 8,444 polysomnograms (Sleep Heart Health Study) and a subjective axis of self-reported…

research.abstract: Background: Cardiovascular epidemiology has long treated "sleep" as a single exposure, although it denotes both an objective physiological state and a subjective behaviour. We tested whether these domains carry separable information about cardiac risk. Methods and Results: We derived an objective axis from 8,444 polysomnograms (Sleep Heart Health Study) and a subjective axis of self-reported duration from 407,303 adults in the 2020 and 2022 Behavioral Risk Factor Surveillance System. Multivariable regression (n=213,489), quadratic dose-response modelling, sleep-stratified comorbidity networks, and era-stratified tests were combined. Objective sleep-disordered breathing was continuous and right-skewed (median apnea-hypopnea index, 31.8 events/h; median sleep efficiency, 69%) in a risk-enriched cohort. Both short (<7 h) and long (>9 h) sleep were associated with disease after full adjustment: adjusted odds ratios for heart attack were 1.24 (95% CI, 1.19-1.30) and 1.30 (1.19-1.42), and for stroke 1.12 (1.06-1.17) and 1.42 (1.29-1.57). A positive quadratic term confirmed a U shape for all 4 outcomes formally tested (P≤6.3×10 2 ), with fitted nadirs of 7.26 to 7.85 hours. Suboptimal sleep also raised comorbidity-network density from 0.089 to 0.112 (short sleep; +26%) and 0.108 (long sleep; +22%), with non-overlapping bootstrap CIs and concordant effects across demographic strata. A survey-weighted replication in official CDC microdata (n=344,010; median design effect, 4.43) preserved the principal cardiac, U-shaped, and network findings; an exploratory COVID-19 interaction (P=0.020) did not survive design-based correction. Conclusions: Objective breathing pathology and subjective duration are separately prognostic, and suboptimal sleep amplifies the cardiometabolic comorbidity network. Duration alone cannot exclude asymptomatic sleep-disordered breathing; cardiovascular prevention should assess both axes.

research.abstract: Abstract Background Group B coxsackieviruses (CVBs) are involved in triggering type 1 diabetes. Free bifidobacterial lipoproteins (BLps) prevent CVBs cell infection. Our objective is to isolate free BLps potentially released by bifidobacteria in breast milk and document their bioavailability. Methods Bifidobacterium breve and B. longum were quantified by qPCR in samples donated to the hospital’s biobank (DHM) within two weeks following delivery. BLps were captured onto CV B4, analyzed by SDS-PAGE and competitive ELISA. BLps transport through Caco-2 monolayers was monitored after DHM contact. Titration of anti-CV B IgA was carried out by ELISA. Results Among the 90 enrolled donors, seven were excluded, 68 donated a unique sample and 15 donated multiple specimens (2 to 12). B. breve and B.longum were detected in 93.0% and 32.8% of unique DHM samples, respectively. The two species showed unstable counts in the multiple donation group. Although at highly variable amounts, BLps were readily detected. Free B.longum Lps were found in absence of B.longum itself. The BLps crossed the cell layer within 4h still binding CV B4. Conclusion DHM contained BLps able to cross a cell layer mimicking the intestine still retaining their capacity to bind CV B. It suggested a possible newborn’s systemic protection against CV B4 infection that needs further investigation.

items.summary: Sex-specific genetic effects on platelet aggregation may contribute to differences in thrombotic risk between women and men, yet the underlying genetic mechanisms remain poorly defined. research.abstract: Abstract Sex-specific genetic effects on platelet aggregation may contribute to differences in thrombotic risk between women and men, yet the underlying genetic mechanisms remain poorly defined. We performed whole-genome sequencing–based genome-wide association studies (GWAS) of 19 harmonized platelet aggregation phenotypes in response to adenosine diphosphate (ADP), epinephrine (EPI), and collagen across three independent cohorts: GeneSTAR, the Framingham Heart Study (FHS) and the Old Order Amish (AMISH). Our meta-GWAS identified a cluster of low-frequency variants within a 20 kb region on chromosome 10 showing strong sex-specific associations with platelet aggregation in response to low-dose EPI. The lead variant, rs116725046, exhibited a genome-wide significant sex interaction (p = 6.7 × 10⁻⁹), with opposite phenotypic effects in women and men. Female carriers demonstrated increased platelet aggregation, whereas male carriers showed decreased aggregation, consistent across cohorts. Several variants in tight linkage disequilibrium with the lead variant yielded additional significant interaction signals for low-dose EPI. The associated variants reside within an intronic region of the long noncoding gene LINC00702 , with FUMA annotations indicating regulatory chromatin states. Megakaryocyte epigenome data also indicates potential regulatory activity in platelet precursor cells in this genomic region. eQTL analyses suggested sex-differentiated genetic regulation of LINC00702 in multiple tissues, with reduced expression in male heterozygotes only. An Androgen Response Element motif was identified upstream of LINC00702 , supporting a potential hormone-responsive regulatory mechanism. Together, these findings identify a novel sex-specific regulatory locus associated with platelet reactivity and highlight LINC00702 as a biologically plausible mediator of sexually dimorphic platelet responses.
