research.abstract: Drug-resistant tuberculosis remains a major challenge in tuberculosis control, and the occurrence of resistance in patients without any prior treatment history raises concern about the transmission of resistant strains within the community.We report the case of a 63-year-old woman presenting with cough for more than two months, marked weight loss, and intermittent fever, without any previous tuberculosis treatment or known contact with a tuberculosis patient.She had a history of diabetes mellitus.Physical examination revealed bronchial breath sounds with rhonchi, and chest radiography revealed infiltration at the right upper lung apex.Rapid molecular testing detected Mycobacterium tuberculosis with resistance to rifampicin, and second-line drug susceptibility testing further revealed additional resistance to isoniazid, fluoroquinolone, and ethionamide, leading to a diagnosis of primary pre-extensively drug-resistant tuberculosis.Random blood glucose was elevated and was managed with insulin, while mild hypochromic anaemia was managed with iron supplementation.The patient received bedaquiline, pretomanid, and linezolid, and remained clinically stable without significant adverse effects after one week of therapy.This case highlights the importance of vigilance for primary drug-resistant tuberculosis and the role of rapid molecular testing in early diagnosis and appropriate treatment selection.

items.title: Population Genomics of the Bovine Sialic Acid Network Reveals Functional and Evolutionary Diversity Across European and South African Cattle Breeds
items.summary: **Background:** Sialic acids, mainly N-acetylneuraminic acid (Neu5Ac) and N-glycolylneuraminic acid (Neu5Gc), are terminal monosaccharides of glycans involved in numerous physiological processes, such as immune and neuronal function. Their biosynthesis, transport, transfer and turnover depend on a network of genes, but genetic studies in cattle have mostly addressed individual genes or genetic…

research.abstract: **Background:** Sialic acids, mainly N-acetylneuraminic acid (Neu5Ac) and N-glycolylneuraminic acid (Neu5Gc), are terminal monosaccharides of glycans involved in numerous physiological processes, such as immune and neuronal function. Their biosynthesis, transport, transfer and turnover depend on a network of genes, but genetic studies in cattle have mostly addressed individual genes or genetic associations with milk oligosaccharide concentrations, leaving variation across this network largely uncharacterized. In bovine milk, sialylated glycans that depend on this network vary among animals and change rapidly during early lactation. We therefore characterized variation in 13 selected genes of the bovine sialic acid network using whole-genome sequence data from European and South African cattle. **Results:** We analyzed 346 animals from 12 European and 4 South African breeds. Of 9,724 variants in the 13 target genes, 8,675 were intronic and 62 were predicted to alter the amino acid sequence. Integration of SIFT predictions, Rate4Site conservation and protein context, with population representation as supporting evidence, identified 15 prioritized candidates, including 7 high-priority candidates in NEU3, ST8SIA2, ST8SIA4, CMAH and ST3GAL4. The most differentiated candidates were not among the 15 prioritized variants. NEU3 Y136H showed the largest regional contrast in allele frequency (0.83 in South African and 0.34 in European cattle), whereas several prioritized candidates were represented by a single allele in the South African cohort. Genome-wide principal component analysis of 950,219 linkage-disequilibrium-pruned SNPs separated South African from European cattle along the first component, which explained about 25% of the variance. None of the 220 analyzed common pathway SNPs exceeded the corresponding genome-wide differentiation thresholds at breed, country or regional level. Within the ascertained pathway SNPs, diversity was higher in South African breeds, and Tajima's D was shifted toward positive values in European breeds and centered near zero in South African breeds. **Conclusions:** This study provides a network-wide map of predicted protein-altering variation in the bovine sialic acid pathway and identifies 15 candidates for functional investigation, most of them rare. Because the most differentiated variants were not those with the strongest functional support, population contrasts, evolutionary conservation and protein context provide complementary evidence for selecting candidates. The analyzed common pathway SNPs did not show exceptional differentiation relative to the genome-wide background. The candidates provide specific targets for genotyping, enzyme-level testing and genotype-informed milk phenotyping.

research.abstract: Abstract Codon-based maximum likelihood models are the workhorse of molecular selection analysis, yet standard workflows assume that the input sequence alignment and phylogenetic tree are known without error. In practice, heuristic aligners ignore the genetic code and phylogeny, which packs non-homologous codons into shared columns across insertion-deletion loops and inflates gene-wide false-positive rates above 80%. This sequential division of labor is statistically suboptimal and computationally wasteful. Here, we present WALRUS ( W heatstone A lignment and L ikelihood R ate U nification for S election), a unified engine in H y P hy 3 ( https://github.com/veg/hyphy-3 ) that maps unaligned coding sequences to a coordinate-consistent selection atlas in one run. From a single Inside–Outside likelihood table, the pipeline repairs reading frames, co-estimates a codon alignment and Ohmic reticulate network, models directional base-composition drift, and evaluates eight selection tests (BUSTED-E, aBSREL, RELAX, FEL, dFEL, MEME, Contrast-FEL, and PRIME). Across 10,020 simulated alignments, WALRUS recovers 94.6% of true columns on the 800 INDELible replicates and cuts indel-driven false positives from 44.7%– 58.1% to 4.4% under BUSTED (21.1%– 21.4% to 1.4% under BUSTED-E). Under Zipfian indel saturation, false positives drop four-fold (33.3%– 83.3% to 17.0%– 20.5%), while 11, 190 avian orthogroup runs execute 6.6–35.8-fold faster and cut housekeeping false positives 13-fold (28-fold on ultraconserved genes) proteome-wide.

research.abstract: Abstract Introduction Hospitals face increasing financial pressures. Hospital reimbursement is tied to the Case Mix Index (CMI). The CMI is a measure of complexity of care provided by the hospital and the total reimbursement is the CMI multiplied by a base pay factor, multiplied by the total number of discharges from the hospital. The few studies in the literature have involved logistically complex attempts to improve documentation. We sought to determine whether limited, structured chart review by surgeons can improve CMI in a multihospital system. Methods We performed a prospective, observational study in a four-hospital academic medical system on all surgical patients from 10/2022 to 7/2026. Two clinically busy trauma surgeons performed limited structured chart reviews for select surgical patients. In the limited intervention period (1/2024-9/2024) this focused only on the trauma division. In the full intervention period (10/2024-7/2026) the review was expanded to all surgical patients across the system. The primary outcome was change in surgical case mix index (CMI) over time. Results A total of 45,559 patients were included (13,807pre-intervention, 9,299 limited intervention, 22,453 full intervention). CMI increased significantly among surgical patients across the whole system (2.83 (95%CI 279-2.87) to 2.86 (95%CI 2.81-2.91) to 2.96 (95%CI 2.93-3.00), ANOVA p <0.001). Overall length of stay was unchanged among surgical patients across the whole system. The estimated increase in revenue per patient attributable to this intervention was $1,765 in surgical patients across the system. Conclusion Having trauma surgeons review targeted surgical patients for high value documentation capture significantly enhanced the CMI and estimated revenue of surgical services across a multi-hospital integrated health system. Such documentation reviews may represent a practical method to improve hospital documentation and revenue. Level of Evidence: Level IV Study Type: Prospective cohort study with historical controls Key Messages What is already known on this topic: Documentation is critically important for hospital billing. Previous studies in trauma and acute care surgery have shown that large, intensive, and dedicated interventions can improve documentation and improve revenue generation. What this study adds: By creating a list of Major Comorbidity/Complication (MCC) and Comorbidity/Complication (CC) codes for targeted review, two clinically busy trauma surgeons were able to perform limited, targeted chart review with significant improvement in DRG capture and Case Mix Index. How this study might affect research, practice or policy: Improvements in documentation are facilitated by the targeted list of MCC and CC codes that other centers can use to improve their DRG capture, further demonstrating the financial benefit of a trauma and acute care surgery service.

research.abstract: Abstract Background Whole-genome sequencing of Mycobacterium tuberculosis (Mtb) commonly relies on culture-derived isolates, potentially altering the bacterial populations represented. Direct sputum whole-genome sequencing (dsWGS) may better capture lineage composition and within-host variant diversity. Methods We compared targeted-enrichment dsWGS with WGS of matched culture-derived isolates from participants initiating treatment for rifampicin-susceptible pulmonary tuberculosis in Worcester, South Africa. We assessed sequencing performance, technical reproducibility, sputum-sampling variability, lineage and variant concordance, and resistance-associated variation, and explored associations with baseline clinical characteristics and treatment response. Results Of 218 clinical dsWGS reactions, 139 passed sequencing quality criteria, yielding 113 eligible baseline sputum–culture pairs. Mixed-lineage infection was detected in 72/113 (63.7%) sputum specimens versus 7/113 (6.2%) matched cultures; 66/113 (58.4%) pairs showed reduced lineage diversity following culture. Permutation analysis indicated preferential retention of Lineage 2 and depletion of Lineage 3 after culture. Technical replicates preserved dominant phylotype assignments (median SNP Jaccard similarity 0.863), while independently collected sputum specimens showed greater variability. Among 38 concordant single-lineage pairs, 35,540/38,311 (92.8%) pair-specific variant observations were shared after filtering and raw-read recovery, while 2,497 (6.5%) were sputum-unique and 274 (0.7%) culture-unique. Discordance was concentrated among variable variants; 88.0% of shared variants variable in at least one specimen had higher allele frequencies in culture. No sputum-unique WHO Grade 1 or 2 resistance-associated mutations were identified in the strain-controlled subset, whereas eight mixed-lineage sputum samples versus three matched cultures harboured such mutations. Higher baseline low-frequency variant burden showed non-significant trends towards delayed culture conversion (log-rank p=0.144) and unfavourable treatment outcomes (log-rank p=0.400). Conclusions Direct-sputum WGS revealed M. tuberculosis lineage and low-frequency variant diversity that was not fully represented by matched culture-derived genomes, despite high overall genomic concordance. These findings highlight the complementary value of direct-sputum sequencing for characterising within-host diversity, while suggesting that the representation of bacterial populations following culture may vary across epidemiological settings. Further research is needed to improve the accuracy of minority-variant detection and establish the clinical relevance of diversity measured directly from sputum.

research.abstract: 32-chain RuNIE phylogenomic and functional selection analysis across 64 species and 16 loci (L = 23,924 aligned columns; African Catarrhini and Neotropical Pitheciidae, Atelidae, Cebidae, Callitrichidae, and Aotidae) coupled with 10,000-generation (20% burn-in) Bayesian coalescent skyline reconstructions across three independent PopSets (Alouatta spp., Sapajus/Cebus, and Callithrix/Saguinus/Leontopithecus) benchmarked against *MAFFT, *IQ-TREE/*LSD2, *PAML codeml, and *BEAST v1.10.4 The colonization of South America by African anthropoid primates during the Middle to Late Eocene and their subsequent diversification across Neotropical forest strata into five ecologically specialized families (Pitheciidae, Atelidae, Cebidae, Callitrichidae, and Aotidae) represent one of mammalogy's classic trans-oceanic adaptive radiations. Here we execute a 32-chain RuNIE phylogenomic and functional selection analysis across a 16-locus, 64-species primate supermatrix (L = 23,924 aligned columns with 10,254 parsimony-informative sites and 11,093 distinct site patterns) coupled with independent 10,000-generation (20% burn-in) Bayesian coalescent skyline reconstructions across three localized Neotropical population datasets benchmarking Native Rust against *MAFFT v7.526, *IQ-TREE v2.4.0 with *LSD2 v2.4.4, *PAML v4.10.10 codeml, and *BEAST v1.10.4. Our fossil-calibrated chronogram anchors Crown Primates at 74.0 Ma, the trans-Atlantic Simiiformes split between African Catarrhini (crown 28.5 Ma) and Neotropical Platyrrhini at 43.2 Ma (stem rafting window 43.2–24.2 Ma across the Eocene Atlantic), and Crown Platyrrhini at 24.2 Ma, followed by crown radiations of Pitheciidae (19.8 Ma), Atelidae (16.8 Ma), Cebidae (19.5 Ma), Callitrichidae (14.8 Ma), and Aotidae (11.4 Ma). Codon selection modeling (*PAML codeml) reveals strong purifying constraint on Pro8-oxytocin OXT/OXTR neuroendocrine signaling (omega = 0.4905), intermediate selective constraint on TAS2R bitter-taste receptors (omega = 0.7442) and ENAM/GHR dental and phyletic-dwarfism loci (omega = 0.8436), and diversifying and balancing selection on duplicated RNASE1/CHIA folivory-insectivory digestive enzymes (omega = 1.2118) and X-linked OPN1LW spectral-tuning opsin exons (omega = 2.4891). Across the three localized PopSet skyline cohorts, we resolve late Quaternary trans-Andean expansion and contemporary yellow fever epizootic pressure in howler monkeys (Alouatta, Ne = 628,056 to 977,186; *BEAST = 1,007,674), Pleistocene Cerrado/Caatinga dry-corridor colonization and stone-tool nut-cracking persistence in capuchins (Sapajus/Cebus, Ne = 1,042,598 to 1,376,278; *BEAST = 1,411,397), and Atlantic Forest fragmentation followed by metapopulation translocation recovery in callitrichid marmosets and tamarins (Callithrix/Saguinus/Leontopithecus, Ne = 469,859 to 912,085; *BEAST = 940,542), while demonstrating that Native Rust achieves a 29.9-fold end-to-end speedup (13.54 s vs. 404.82 s Hybrid and 3127.88 s full External UFBoot). research.abstract: ABSTRACT RfaH, a member of the universally conserved NusG/Spt5 family, activates transcription and translation of virulence genes by bridging the transcribing RNA polymerase to the translating ribosome. Unlike its monomorphic, constitutively active paralog NusG, RfaH fold-switches from an autoinhibited state, wherein its C-terminal domain forms an α-helical hairpin bound to the N-terminal domain, into an active NusG-like state through C-terminal domain dissociation and refolding into a β-barrel. RfaH has been proposed to evolve from NusG via gene duplication by first activating genes adjacent to its production site, before developing autoinhibition to selectively control distant genes. Using AlphaFold2, we predicted the structures of thousands of RfaH homologs and identified a subset (∼14%) that appear predominantly folded in the active state. In vivo assays confirmed that these putative monomorphic homologs exhibit constitutive activity comparable to known RfaH mutants. Phylogenetic and genomic analyses revealed that these monomorphic proteins form a distinct clade and are preferentially located within or next to long virulence-associated operons. Together, these results further support a stepwise evolutionary model of RfaH specialization through structural transformation.

research.abstract: Abstract Background The HSP70 family maintains cellular proteostasis and mediates vertebrate responses to environmental stress. The Chinese alligator ( Alligator sinensis ), an ectothermic crocodilian, undergoes winter dormancy characterized by cessation of feeding, reduced activity, and metabolic depression. However, the evolutionary patterns of the HSP70 family across vertebrates and their potential relevance to winter dormancy in crocodilians remain poorly understood. We characterized the HSP70 family across 24 vertebrate species, focusing on the molecular evolution of HSPA12A along crocodilian lineages and its seasonal expression in the hypothalamus of the Chinese alligator. Results Using HMMER- and BLAST-based searches, we identified 355 HSP70 family members, with 11–28 members per species. Phylogenetic, synteny, and subcellular localization analyses indicated that the family is broadly conserved but exhibits subfamily- and lineage-associated divergence. Under two foreground schemes in which the terminal branches of two winter-dormant crocodilians or all four crocodilian species were jointly designated as foreground, HSPA12A showed an elevated relative evolutionary rate and significant evidence of positive selection. HyPhy aBSREL supported episodic diversifying selection on the A. sinensis HSPA12A terminal branch. Public RNA-seq data showed that HSPA12A expression was highest in the hypothalamus among sampled female tissues and was higher in winter than in summer (600.0 and 329.2 TPM, respectively). Western blotting and immunofluorescence analyses showed descriptive differences between the examined specimens, with higher HSPA12A protein abundance and a higher density of cells double-positive for anti-HSPA12A antibody immunoreactivity and NeuN in winter. Because each RNA-seq, western blotting, and immunofluorescence comparison included only one biological specimen per season, these observations were treated as descriptive, and no inferential statistical comparisons were performed. Conclusions The vertebrate HSP70 family is broadly conserved but shows differentiation among subfamilies and lineages. The evolutionary analyses indicate a broader crocodilian-lineage-associated pattern of HSPA12A evolution that cannot be attributed specifically to winter dormancy. Separately, the descriptive transcriptomic and preliminary protein-level observations provide a basis for considering HSPA12A as a candidate for further investigation in relation to winter physiology in the Chinese alligator. These findings do not establish winter dormancy as the selective driver of HSPA12A evolution, and its biological function and causal role remain to be determined.

authors.affiliation: Department of Clinical Sciences, Faculty of Veterinary and Animal Sciences, University of Layyah, Layyah, 31200, Pakistan

research.abstract: Camelids have evolved remarkable physiological adaptations enabling survival in extreme desert environments, yet the genomic basis of these traits remains incompletely understood. We conducted a comparative genomic analysis across eleven mammalian species, including three Old World camels, four New World camels, two additional artiodactyls (pig, cattle), and two outgroups (human, mouse), to identify lineage-specific molecular signatures of adaptation. Using OrthoFinder, we constructed orthologous gene families and identified 11,861 single-copy orthologs across all species. We detected significant copy-number changes in cytochrome P450 gene families, with expansion of CYP2J and contraction of CYP4F in the camelid ancestor, suggesting a shift toward anti-inflammatory eicosanoid signaling. Branch-site analyses identified 47 high-confidence positively selected genes in Old World camels, including HACD3, a fatty acid elongation enzyme harboring an ultraconserved substitution (D270N). Structural modeling and conservation analysis suggest that this substitution may hypothetically alter protein conformation, but this prediction awaits experimental validation. Tissue-specific RNA-seq analysis confirmed that HACD3 is expressed in camel kidney and liver, tissues central to lipid metabolism and water conservation. Systematic screening for inactivating mutations identified ten high-confidence pseudogenized genes, including CES3, CPA3, and PLA2G2F, enriched in lipid metabolism and epidermal pathways. The adaptive significance of these losses is currently hypothetical and inferred from homologous gene studies in mice and humans; because some of the cited genes are paralogs rather than orthologs, and because mouse and human phenotypes may not transfer to camels, these inferences are hypothesis-generating only and do not establish camel gene function. Experimental validation confirmed pseudogenization of TAS2R16, and cell-based calcium-signalling assays showed that the camel receptor fails to respond to salicin. This establishes loss of receptor function but not its adaptive significance; both dietary-breadth and neutral (relaxed-selection or drift) explanations remain compatible with the data. For CES3, CPA3, and PLA2G2F, functional consequences in camels remain unverified and require camel-specific experimental validation. Collectively, these results provide a comprehensive framework of gene family evolution, positive selection, and gene loss underlying desert adaptation in camelids, while highlighting that expression patterns are correlative only and do not demonstrate that the identified variants alter protein function or physiology.

research.abstract: Abstract Thienothiazolocarboxamides (TTCs) were discovered as a hit in a whole cell screen for new antituberculosis agents. These molecules were rapidly cidal under both replicating and non-replicating conditions and killed Mycobacterium tuberculosis (Mtb) in macrophages. The heterobicyclic core of this scaffold was essential for activity and resistance to these agents was mediated by loss of EthA, a flavin containing monooxygenase also responsible for the bioactivation of ethionamide. EthA-mediated activation of TTCs in whole cells was found to produce mycothiol adducts and RNAseq profiles revealed a mechanism of action identical to the fungal mycotoxins patulin and nidulalin A. EthA oxidizes the sulfur of the thiazole ring to create a relatively stable sulfenic acid that reacts with cellular thiols. This unique, replication-independent, mechanism suggests the possibility that these molecules may contribute significantly to shortening the duration of tuberculosis chemotherapy.

research.abstract: Abstract Background Dosing guidance for children with leprosy remains operationally challenging. For children under 10 years of age, current WHO recommendations rely on mg/kg dosing of the three separate components of leprosy multidrug therapy, which are difficult to implement in routine care and may result in inconsistent drug exposures. Weight-banded dosing offers a pragmatic alternative that better aligns with pharmacokinetic principles and existing drug formulations. Methodology A pharmacokinetic simulation study was conducted to develop harmonized weight-banded dosing regimens for rifampicin, clofazimine, and dapsone in children aged 2 to 10 years. Using the WHO dosing tool, drug exposures across harmonized weight bands were simulated and adult-equivalent systemic exposure (80–125% of adult area under the concentration–time curve) targeted. Predicted exposures were contextualized against safety reference regimens used in tuberculosis meningitis, multidrug-resistant tuberculosis, and leprosy. An iterative review process involving the WHO Technical Working Group on leprosy in children ensured clinical and operational feasibility. Results Proposed weight-banded multidrug therapy regimens achieved adult-equivalent exposures across most weight bands. Predicted exposures modestly exceeded 125% of adult levels at the lower end of selected weight bands but remained well below safety benchmarks, namely exposures associated with daily rifampicin therapy for tuberculosis meningitis and clofazimine regimens for multidrug-resistant tuberculosis. Dapsone exposures were comparable to those achieved with current leprosy dosing. The existing 10–14-year-old child MDT blister pack could be used without modification in children weighing 25–39.9 kg and with limited tablet or gel capsule removal in children weighing 6–24.9 kg. Conclusions A harmonized weight-banded dosing strategy was developed that enables effective, practical dosing of leprosy multidrug therapy in children under 10 years using existing free-of-charge blister packs provided through WHO. This approach improves dosing consistency, supports programmatic implementation, and provides a rational interim solution while child-friendly formulations are being developed. Author Summary Leprosy continues to affect children in many low-resource settings, yet guidance on how to dose treatment in younger children remains limited. Current recommendations often require clinicians to calculate mg/kg doses, which can be difficult in practice and may not match the oral formulations that are available. In this study, we used computer-based simulations to develop a simplified dosing approach for the three drugs used to treat leprosy. We showed that grouping children into weight bands, rather than calculating individual doses, can achieve drug exposures similar to those seen in adults, where treatment is known to be effective. Importantly, we found that these doses can be delivered using existing pre-packed treatment kits by removing selected dose units, making this approach practical in routine care. This work provides a more straightforward and reliable way to treat children with leprosy, reducing the burden on clinicians and improving access to treatment. However, challenges remain, including the lack of child-friendly formulations and limited data on how these drugs behave in children. Further studies are needed to improve treatment for this vulnerable population.

research.abstract: IntroductionAntimicrobial resistance (AMR) to first line antibiotics for pneumonia is a major global health problem, and AMR-attributable deaths are prevalent in sub-Saharan Africa. Improved data on how AMR develops and influences health outcomes in resource limited settings is crucial. The nasopharynx is a reservoir for pneumonia pathogens and their resistome, the genetic determinants of AMR. No study has explored whether human resistome composition in children with pneumonia is associated with health outcomes. This study will examine whether antibiotic treatment and hospital admission for pneumonia generate a persistent hospital-acquired nasopharyngeal resistome in children, and whether this is associated with re-hospitalisation. MethodsThis is an observational case-control study, that will recruit 350 children aged 12-36 months from four groups in Blantyre, Malawi: healthy children in the community (healthy community), children with pneumonia treated in the community (community pneumonia), children hospitalised with pneumonia (hospital pneumonia) and children re-hospitalised with pneumonia (re-hospitalised pneumonia). Nasopharyngeal swabs will be taken at recruitment and 3-month follow-up study visits for metagenomic sequencing to characterise the nasopharyngeal microbiome and resistome; urine samples will be taken at recruitment for an antibiotic activity bioassay. Socio-demographic data, co-morbidities, pneumonia severity, antibiotic exposure and health outcomes will be recorded. AnalysisCross-sectional comparisons between groups at recruitment will examine whether nasopharyngeal resistome (NPR) composition differs by pneumonia severity, antibiotic and healthcare exposure. Longitudinal comparisons within groups will assess the dynamics of NPR composition over time. The study is powered to detect a medium effect size (Cohens D = 0.505) change in the relative abundance of antibiotic resistance genes (ARGs) between all four groups. Primary outcomes are the difference in beta diversity (Bray-Curtis dissimilarity index), and relative abundance of ARG classes in the NPR. The primary objectives are to estimate the difference in diversity and relative abundance of the NPR between hospitalised pneumonia participants when compared to 1) healthy community and 2) community pneumonia participants, and to investigate whether participants re-hospitalised with pneumonia within a 3-month period have a persistent hospital-acquired NPR pattern. Ethics and disseminationThe study has been approved by the Kamuzu University of Heath Sciences Research Ethics Committee (KUREC, formerly Malawi College of Medicine Research Ethics Committee; Ref: P.10/24-1200) and Liverpool School of Tropical Medicine Research Ethics Committee (LSTM REC; Ref: 24-076). Trial registration numberISRCTN64027792 STRENGTHS AND LIMITATIONS OF THIS STUDYO_ST_ABSStrengthsC_ST_ABSO_LIStudy design that uses metagenomic deep sequencing to enable direct, concurrent comparison of nasopharyngeal microbiome (NPM) and resistome (NPR) composition between community and hospitalised paediatric populations with pneumonia in a resource-limited setting. C_LIO_LIData on reported and urinary bioassay-detected antibiotic use prior to, and throughout the study, enabling detailed examination of antibiotic selective pressure on the NPR. C_LIO_LIInvestigation of the association between NPR composition and adverse clinical outcomes from pneumonia. C_LI LimitationsO_LILimitations to this study include few sampling time points (two for community pneumonia and three for hospitalised pneumonia), which may not fully capture the impact of antibiotic exposure; the potential for residual confounding following adjustment for known potential confounders (e.g. age, sex, co-morbidities, household exposure to smoke and breastfeeding) in the association between resistome composition and adverse clinical outcomes, for which the authors have detailed statistical analysis measures; and ability to only determine association between NPR composition and adverse clinical outcomes, rather than causal inference, due to the case-control study design. C_LI SUMMARYO_ST_ABSWhat is already known on this topicC_ST_ABSThe nasopharynx is a reservoir for pneumonia pathogens and their genetic determinants of antibiotic resistance in children. Studies of nasopharyngeal microbiome composition have shown association with paediatric pneumonia severity and mortality. What this study addsThis study will describe nasopharyngeal resistome (NPR) evolution under selective pressure of antibiotics and hospitalisation for paediatric pneumonia, and explore whether NPR composition is associated with health outcomes in a resource-limited setting. How this study might affect research, practice or policyThis exploratory study could inform larger scale observational studies to examine the association between antibiotic resistance and health outcomes, by defining high-risk nasopharyngeal resistome composition, helping to determine the required sample size and contributing open-source bioinformatic pipelines. The study could also inform research for public health interventions, including antibiotic stewardship.

research.abstract: ABSTRACT Synonymous codon usage bias (CUB) provides a complementary perspective on molecular variation, but its relationship with morphological diversity in rapidly radiating plant lineages remains poorly understood. We investigated this relationship in Thelypteridaceae by integrating chloroplast phylogenomics, codon usage analyses, and published descriptions of lamina base architecture. A phylogeny based on 31 shared protein‐coding genes provided the evolutionary framework for 37 plastome accessions, including two outgroups. Uniform Manifold Approximation and Projection (UMAP) revealed three major codon usage groupings (Types A–C) that partly differed from the chloroplast phylogeny, with Types A and C corresponding descriptively to contrasting lamina base forms. A focused comparison of 27 accessions and eight genes retained this Type A–Type C separation. Although ENC, PR2, and neutrality plots showed broadly similar overall patterns between the types, gene‐wise analyses highlighted ndhJ, psaA, and psbD, and protein‐guided codon alignments reproduced their type‐specific synonymous third‐position counts. These complementary observations support a relationship between chloroplast codon usage variation and frond architecture in the sampled taxa. They identify candidate photosynthesis‐related loci and provide a basis for testing the evolutionary and functional processes underlying this relationship.

research.abstract: Mycobacterium tuberculosis infects the lungs and causes the disease tuberculosis, which the World Health Organization estimates causes 1 million deaths across the globe annually. Emergence of drug resistance has lessened the effectiveness and requires a longer duration of treatment. Bedaquiline was approved by the FDA in 2012 to treat multi-drug-resistant tuberculosis cases when no other treatment was viable. TBAJ-587, a derivative of Bedaquiline, has been found to be more effective at treating multi-drug-resistant tuberculosis, and has fewer adverse effects. The aim of this project was to test if strains of Mycobacterium tuberculosis that have a mutation in Rv0678 causing overexpression of the MmpS5L5 efflux pump will evolve high-level resistance to TBAJ-587 at a higher frequency than wild-type strains. This was done by growing a wild-type M. tuberculosis strain and a ∆Rv0678 mutant on plates of 7H11 agar containing increasing concentrations of TBAJ-587, then selecting isolates and confirming resistance using an anti-microbial susceptibility assay to determine the Minimum Inhibitory Concentration of the isolated strains. 72 strains from the wild-type background were assayed, and 114 from the ∆Rv0678 background were assayed. The resistant ∆Rv0678 strains tended to have higher minimum inhibitory concentrations that the resistant WT strains. Mutations in the WT strains were found throughout Rv0678, and D28, E6, A62 and I66 mutations in atpE, as well as L168 in atpB. Similar atpE mutations were found in ∆Rv0678, with the addition of mutations in A63 of atpE.

research.abstract: Abstract Background Childhood respiratory infectious deaths are partitioned across four Global Burden of Disease cause modules—26 etiological attributions within lower respiratory infections, tuberculosis, COVID-19, and whooping cough—never jointly reported. Whether the structure of this combined mortality spectrum has changed over time, and with what implications for intervention design, has not been quantified. We assembled and analyzed the integrated spectrum for children and adolescents aged 0– 19 years, 1990–2023. Methods We integrated Global Burden of Disease Study 2023 (release v8352) estimates into a 29-node spectrum—26 lower respiratory infection etiologies plus tuberculosis, COVID-19, and pertussis— globally and across seven super-regions, with uncertainty propagated by summing bounds. We computed Shannon diversity, Herfindahl concentration, and effective cause counts; phenotyped pandemic-window collapse and rebound per cause; linked pathogen shares to WHO/UNICEF vaccine coverage; and mapped geographic concentration in sub-Saharan Africa and South Asia. Segmented (joinpoint) log-linear models with breakpoints selected by the Bayesian information criterion were fitted to annual totals, Shannon diversity and leading pathogen shares. Results In 2023 the 29 causes jointly accounted for 965,330 deaths (95% uncertainty interval [UI] 680,096–1,342,437). Shannon diversity rose from 2.336 to 2.711 (+16.1%) between 1990 and 2023; the effective number of causes nearly doubled (5.57 to 9.94), inversely coupled to total deaths (Spearman ρ = −0.997). Whooping cough ranked second (112,954 deaths; 95% UI 64,576–185,708; 11.7%) and showed the spectrum’s only rebound above 100% (−57.4% collapse, +111.0% rebound). Tuberculosis ranked third (87,764; 57,779–124,912; 9.1%) with the highest concentration in sub-Saharan Africa and South Asia (87.1%). COVID-19 entered at rank five (52,899; 47,275–59,183; 5.5%). Nineteen of 29 causes exceeded the poverty-lock threshold (>80.59% of deaths in sub-Saharan Africa plus South Asia). Joinpoint analysis placed breakpoints in total deaths at 2011, 2018 and 2021—the decline slowed from −3.4% to −2.3% per year after 2011, steepened to −7.1% per year in 2018–2021 and rebounded +4.5% per year in 2021–2023—while diversification accelerated to +1.18% per year in 2013–2020; all six leading pathogen shares carried a pandemic-window breakpoint at 2019 and 2021 (S. pneumoniae at 2018 and 2021). Conclusions Childhood respiratory infectious mortality has become more diverse and more concentrated in poverty as it has declined. Single-pathogen interventions now address a shrinking share; the spectrum’s structure argues for platform interventions—oxygen, antimicrobial access, referral—tailored jointly by age and geography, implying that pathogen-specific strategies alone cannot finish the remaining mortality agenda.

items.summary: BackgroundApolipoprotein B (apoB) and low-density lipoprotein cholesterol (LDL-C) are established biomarkers of atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease (ASCVD) that tend to be closely correlated. research.abstract: Abstract Background Apolipoprotein B (apoB) and low-density lipoprotein cholesterol (LDL-C) are established biomarkers of atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease (ASCVD) that tend to be closely correlated. However, some individuals have discordant apoB and LDL-C. We evaluated whether apoB/LDL-C discordance is associated with elevated high-sensitivity C-reactive protein (hs-CRP), a key marker of systemic inflammation, in a nationally representative sample. Methods and Results We analyzed cross-sectional data of 2226 adults aged 20 years or older from the 2015 to 2016 National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey with complete apoB, LDL-C, and high-sensitivity C-reactive protein (hs-CRP). LDL-C and apoB were converted to survey-weighted z scores, and discordance was the residual of apoB regressed on LDL-C. Participants were classified as apoB-high, LDL-C-high, or concordant (reference). The association of discordance group with elevated hs-CRP ( > 3 mg/L) was estimated with survey-weighted logistic regression, adjusted for age, sex, body mass index (BMI), and diabetes. Discordance was present in 26.4% of adults (13.7% apoB-higher, 12.6% LDL-C-higher). Elevated hs-CRP prevalence differed by discordance group: 47.6% (95% CI, 37.6–57.7) in the apoB-high group versus 20.5% (12.9–28.1) in the LDL-C-high group and 33.6% (29.7–37.4) in the concordant group. Relative to concordant participants, adjusted odds of elevated hs-CRP were higher for apoB-high discordance (odds ratio [OR], 1.58; 95% CI, 1.03–2.45) and lower for LDL-C-high discordance (OR, 0.49; 95% CI, 0.30–0.78). Similar results were obtained among participants not on statin therapy, with apoB-high discordance demonstrating stronger adjusted odds of elevated hs-CRP (OR, 2.02; 95% CI, 1.01–4.04). Conclusion Discordantly high apoB relative to LDL-C is associated with systemic inflammation in a nationally representative sample of U.S. adults.

research.abstract: Background: Swab-based molecular testing for tuberculosis (TB) could provide a near point-of-care (nPOC) diagnostic for children. We evaluated the accuracy of two swab-based nPOC platforms to detect pediatric pulmonary TB. Methods: We prospectively enrolled children under 15 years with presumptive TB in Uganda and South Africa. They completed TB evaluation including sputum molecular testing and culture. Two tongue swabs were collected and tested with MiniDock MTB (Pluslife Biotech, China) and Truenat MTB Ultima (Molbio Diagnostics, India), and one swab was dipped in sputum for testing with MiniDock MTB. We calculated the sensitivity and specificity of each index test against a culture-based standard and compared them with sputum molecular testing and smear microscopy. Findings: We included 335 children, among whom median age was 3 years (IQR 1-6), 53% were female, 11% were living with HIV, and 16% had microbiologically confirmed TB. Tongue swabs were collected in all children, with invalid test rates of less than 3%. Against a culture-based standard, the sensitivities of tongue swab MiniDock MTB and MTB Ultima were 50% (95% CI 33.4-66.6) and 50% (95% CI 28.2-71.8), respectively, and specificities were [≥]98% for both. Sputum swab MiniDock MTB had similar sensitivity to sputum Xpert Ultra (85.7% vs. 75.0%, p=0.45), but substantially higher sensitivity than tongue swab MiniDock MTB (+23.1%, p=0.03) and sputum smear microscopy (+46.4%, p<0.001). Interpretation: Sputum swab testing had similar accuracy to sputum Xpert Ultra in children. Tongue swab testing had moderate accuracy, and has value to identify microbiologically confirmed cases when sputum is not available.

research.abstract: Abstract Cytochrome P450 (CYP) genes form a large and functionally diverse superfamily of heme-thiolate monooxygenases that catalyse the oxidation of endogenous and exogenous compounds. Within this superfamily, CYP4 enzymes primarily act on fatty acids, substrates central to energy metabolism. Sustained flight and long distance migration in birds rely on efficient fatty acid use, making CYP4 a pertinent system for examining how lipid associated functions may vary across avian lineages. Here, we characterised the evolution of CYP4 genes across 363 avian whole genomes, representing over 90% of bird families, to investigate patterns of molecular evolution and their association with ecological and life history variation. We identified four CYP4 subfamilies and analysed sequence evolution using site-models, branch-models, and branch-site models. Our analyses revealed conserved elements of the avian CYP4 repertoire alongside lineage-specific heterogeneity in selective constraint. Several amino acid sites under positive selection were located within substrate recognition sites, regions influencing substrate binding and catalysis. Branch-model analyses identified trait-associated variation in selective pressure across feeding habits, migration and primary lifestyle, with gene-specific patterns. Migration-associated differences in ω remained below one, indicating variation in the strength of selective constraint among migration categories. Branch-site analyses revealed evidence of episodic positive selection associated with migratory lineages. Overall, these results highlight site-specific adaptive evolution within CYP4 genes alongside broader variation in selective constraint, providing insight into the evolution of lipid associated metabolic pathways during avian diversification.

research.abstract: Abstract Introduction: Hepatic tuberculosis is a rare extrapulmonary manifestation that may mimic hepatobiliary malignancy or complex cystic lesions, resulting in diagnostic challenges. Case Presentation: A 36-year-old Filipino woman without recognized immunocompromising conditions presented with fever, weight loss, jaundice, and right upper quadrant pain. Imaging showed a multiloculated cystic lesion in hepatic segments V/VI with focal biliary prominence. Liver biopsy demonstrated necrotizing and non-necrotizing granulomatous inflammation with focally positive Ziehl-Neelsen staining. Tissue MTB-PCR detected Mycobacterium tuberculosis without rifampicin resistance, and culture confirmed M. tuberculosis complex susceptible to streptomycin, isoniazid, rifampicin, and ethambutol. CT chest showed diffuse bilateral micronodules in a miliary pattern; initial sputum smear and PCR were negative, but final sputum culture became positive at 6 weeks. Standard 2HRZE/4HR therapy was initiated, with clinical and biochemical improvement at 1 month. Conclusion: Hepatic tuberculosis should be considered in atypical cystic hepatic lesions, and tissue diagnosis is essential to avoid unnecessary invasive procedures.

research.abstract: Bacterial flagella are rotary nanomachines that enable motility in diverse environments. Although more than 40 genes are required for a functional flagellum in model organisms, only 24 have previously been inferred to be ancestral. Did the last bacterial common ancestor (LBCA) encode a simpler flagellum that was subsequently elaborated, or has its complexity been underestimated because highly diverged homologs are difficult to detect? Here, we combine homology searches across 80,789 bacterial proteomes with conserved sequence signatures, gene-tree clustering, and gene-neighborhood evidence to reconstruct the ancestral flagellum. We identify 49 flagellar protein groups with high-confidence support for ancestral presence across three phylogenetic reconstructions and one additional likely ancestral component, yielding a reconstructed repertoire of 50 ancestral protein groups. This repertoire includes the major structural, export, motor, and assembly components required for a functional flagellum. We provide an interactive database (https://www.flagelladb.org) for exploring the distribution, co-presence, and phylogenetic relationships of flagellar components across bacteria. Our findings indicate that the LBCA possessed a complex, functionally complete flagellar system, substantially exceeding previous estimates of ancestral complexity. The distribution of these components among extant bacteria is consistent with extensive lineage-specific loss and remodeling during subsequent flagellar evolution.

research.abstract: BackgroundLinkage of infectious-disease surveillance data to mortality records is important for estimating long-term outcomes, but incomplete personal identifiers present methodological challenges. We developed and validated a deterministic linkage framework for linking the National Tuberculosis Surveillance System (NTBS) with Office for National Statistics (ONS) mortality records. MethodsTB notifications in England from 2001-2024 were linked to ONS mortality records using 12 sequential matching rules based on combinations of NHS number, date of birth, name, postcode, sex and phonetic matching. Linkage outputs underwent person-level deduplication and clerical review. Precision and recall were estimated, and potential linkage bias assessed by variation in identifier completeness and linkage success. Confirmed false-positive links identified during validation were removed from the analytical dataset. ResultsAmong 151,965 TB notifications, 28,060 initial links were identified. Following deduplication, validation and refinement, 26,937 linked notifications were retained. Estimated precision increased from 97.7% to 99.2% (95% CI 96.8-100.0) following removal of false-positive links; estimated recall was 98.1% (95% CI 95.4-98.6%). More than 90% of links used NHS-number-based match keys. PDS enrichment increased NHS-number availability and enabled additional NHS-number-based links, although a small proportion linked to different ONS records following enrichment. NHS number availability and linkage success differed across demographic and social groups, demonstrating differential linkage. ConclusionsA hierarchical deterministic approach combined with targeted validation achieved high linkage accuracy while identifying and addressing differential linkage. This provides a transparent framework for future NTBS-ONS linkage and may be adaptable to other surveillance systems where comparable identifiers are available. Key messagesO_LIHierarchical deterministic linkage achieved high precision (>99%) and recall (>96%) when linking tuberculosis notifications to mortality records. C_LIO_LIValidation demonstrated that high linkage accuracy can be achieved using routinely collected identifiers within national surveillance data. C_LIO_LIThe validated linkage provides a robust framework for mortality ascertainment and long-term outcome monitoring within tuberculosis surveillance. C_LI

research.abstract: Acrosin (ACR) and transmembrane protease serine 12 (TMPRSS12) are sperm-related S1/trypsin-like serine proteases involved in mammalian male fertility, but their evolutionary relationship in vertebrates remains unclear. Here, we combined phylogenetic, synteny, selection-pressure, and transcriptomic analyses to investigate their evolutionary origin and divergence. OHNOLOGS v2 identified ACR-TMPRSS12 as a candidate ohnolog pair with strong outgroup support, and OrthoFinder placed their duplication in the ancestor of jawed vertebrates. Phylogenetic analyses recovered ACR and TMPRSS12 as reciprocally monophyletic sister clades, consistent with an ancient duplication that may be associated with the two rounds of whole-genome duplication (2R-WGD). Their subsequent evolutionary trajectories differed markedly. ACR was retained in chondrichthyans, sarcopterygians, tetrapods, and acipenseriforms, whereas its widespread loss in other actinopterygians largely coincided with acrosome loss, although bichirs retained the acrosome but lacked ACR. TMPRSS12 was widely retained across jawed vertebrates but showed relaxed selection in Poeciliidae and independent losses in Sebastes and Takifugu. Both genes exhibited testis-biased transcript expression, and their proteins retained a relatively conserved trypsin-like catalytic domain. These findings reveal contrasting patterns of gene retention between ACR and TMPRSS12 and lineage-specific variation in selective constraints on TMPRSS12, consistent with their divergence following an ancient duplication event.

research.abstract: Background Mycobacterium tuberculosis (Mtb), the causative agent of tuberculosis (TB) is able to survive and replicate within host cells of the myeloid cell lineage, a critical step in the development of active TB, achieved through multiple immune evasion mechanisms. TRPML1 (Mucolipin 1), a non-selective Ca 2+ ion channel belonging to the TRP superfamily, is predominantly expressed in innate immune cells and is localized intracellularly along the endosomal–lysosomal continuum. TRPML1-mediated Ca 2+ signalling is vital for lysosomal biogenesis and trafficking processes essential for effective immune responses. The mechanisms regulating TRPML1 channel function in myeloid cells during mycobacterial infection remain poorly characterized. Methods During in vitro infection, TRPML1 expression was modulated in a time-dependent manner by Mtb and M. bovis BCG in murine macrophages, as well as in human neutrophils (PMNs) and macrophages (MDMs). Using pharmacological modulation of TRPML1 channel activity, we observed alterations in intracellular Ca 2+ concentrations following Mtb infection. Results Here, we describe distinct TRPML1 expression patterns in granulomas from TB patients who had completed treatment for active TB, suggesting a potential role for TRPML1 in pathogenesis. We further demonstrate that Mtb infection is associated with altered TRPML1 expression and intracellular Ca 2+ homeostasis, accompanied by changes in ROS production, necrotic cell death and enhanced mycobacterial survival within host cells. Treatment of PMN-MDM cocultures with a TRPML1 antagonist, but not an agonist, was associated with increased reactive oxygen species (ROS) levels and necrotic cell death. Discussion Here, we show that Mtb-mediated disruption of TRPML1 function is associated with altered intracellular Ca 2+ homeostasis and may contribute to impaired phagosome maturation, a process previously linked to TRPML1-dependent endolysosomal function, thereby potentially favoring mycobacterial survival within host cells. These findings suggest that Mtb-induced alterations in TRPML1 associated cellular Ca²⁺ homeostasis may impair Ca²⁺-dependent ROS production and cell death, potentially affecting intracellular Mtb survival. Our findings support a role for TRPML1 in maintaining myeloid cell Ca²⁺ homeostasis and suggest that TRPML1 may contribute to the innate immune response to Mtb infection.

research.abstract: Abstract Mycobacterium tuberculosis withstands acidic conditions to survive and replicate within macrophages. To define the genetic determinants of this adaptation, we performed a transposon screen in a lipid-rich, acidic medium that mimics the host environment and supports robust M. tuberculosis growth. This screen identified ldtB , encoding an L,D-transpeptidase, as essential for growth and survival under acid stress. Loss of LdtB decreased 3–3 peptidoglycan cross-linking, disrupted cell wall architecture, and impaired intrabacterial pH homeostasis, resulting in increased susceptibility to cell wall–active antibiotics. Notably, M. tuberculosis lacking LdtB displayed heightened sensitivity to meropenem within macrophages, suggesting that targeting this enzyme could potentiate β-lactam efficacy during infection. These findings establish LdtB as a key mediator linking peptidoglycan homeostasis to acid stress resistance and underscores the importance of in vitro culture models that recapitulate the host microenvironment for uncovering new in vivo active therapeutic targets. Teaser Disabling a key peptidoglycan cross-linking enzyme compromises M. tuberculosis survival under acidic stress and antibiotic exposure.

research.abstract: ABSTRACT Background Tuberculosis (TB) notifications have increased in several high-income countries since 2020. Proposed explanations include pandemic-related disruption of treatment for latent tuberculosis, changes in population composition, and immune dysfunction following SARS-CoV-2 infection. We assessed whether TB presentations increased during the pandemic era and then tested whether community SARS-CoV-2 activity was followed by increased mycobacterial disease. Methods We conducted a population-based ecological time-series study of first TB- and nontuberculous mycobacterial (NTM)-coded hospital, emergency-department and ambulatory-clinic presentations in the Greater Toronto–Hamilton Area Plus (GTHA+), Ontario (2024 population approximately 11.2 million), from April 2011 through March 2024. NTM served as a comparator because it shares diagnostic pathways with TB but differs epidemiologically. Negative-binomial projection and full-series models estimated pandemic-era changes under three alternative trend assumptions. Distributed lag non-linear models estimated cumulative rate ratios for standardized community viral activity over 0–12 weeks; sensitivity analyses extended the maximum lag to 26 and 52 weeks. Influenza and respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) were prespecified comparators; data for five additional viral exposures were obtained after the primary analysis was completed and analysed as exploratory comparisons. Results We identified 3,985 first TB-coded and 5,214 first NTM-coded acute-care presentations. Across six models, estimated pandemic-era TB increases ranged from 3% to 22%. No model suggested an increased in NTM. SARS-CoV-2 activity was not positively associated with TB (cumulative rate ratio per 1-SD increase over 0–12 weeks 0.909, 95% CI 0.822–1.006) or NTM (0.953, 0.868–1.047). No positive associations were identified in subgroup analyses or with maximum lags of 26 or 52 weeks. Influenza was not associated with either outcome. RSV was associated with TB and NTM; only the RSV–NTM association met the Bonferroni threshold among the prespecified comparisons, and no exploratory associations met the experiment-wide threshold. Conclusions We identified a modest pandemic-era increase in TB-coded acute-care presentations in Ontario, Canada, although its estimated size depended on assumptions about underlying trends. NTM-coded presentations did not increase. Community SARS-CoV-2 activity was not positively associated with subsequent TB or NTM presentations at lags of up to one year and did not provide a temporal explanation for the population-level TB increase. Individual-level effects cannot be excluded.

research.abstract: Abstract Infectious diseases continue to pose a global health challenge, intensified by antimicrobial resistance and limitations of pharmaceutical countermeasures. Nanotechnology offers a promising front against these barriers using intelligent, multifunctional systems. This review explores the convergence of Artificial Intelligence (AI), CRISPR gene editing, bacteriophage therapy, and immune modulation within the framework of second-generation nanoparticle therapeutics. AI-guided modelling enables predictive optimization of nanoparticle design on the basis of size, charge, and surface proteins, targeting specific pathogens and providing enhanced stability. Consequently, nanoparticles serve as precision nanocarriers and protective delivery vehicles for the CRISPR-Cas system, shielding nucleic acid cargo from enzymatic degradation and enabling targeted intracellular delivery via pH-responsive endosomal escape mechanisms. The nanoparticles not only provide protection but also enable tissue-targeting and infection-site-specific delivery of the CRISPR-Cas system, facilitating precise genome editing to reverse resistance in specific pathogens such as HIV and Mycobacterium tuberculosis. Phage nanoparticle hybrids further expand antimicrobial potency by enhancing phage stability, delivery, and host range. Moreover, engineered nanoparticles modulate the immune system via immunosuppressive and immunostimulant strategies for reducing hyperinflammation and enhancing pathogen clearance, respectively. Despite such encouraging laboratory outcomes, the clinical translation of AI-integrated nanoparticle platforms still faces a number of obstacles. Large-scale manufacturing, scalability, and reproducibility pose a significant challenge. Regulatory approvals for such multi-modal nano-drugs seem to get bogged down due to vague and scarce exemplary proofs. Furthermore, safety and efficacy apprehensions, unpredictable and complex host-phage interactions, cost-effectiveness, and equitable access remain a subject matter of concern. Conclusively, the convergence of advanced nanotechnology, artificial intelligence, and synthetic biology marks the dawn of a transformative era in infectious disease therapeutics where treatment is not only intelligent and adaptive but also ethically and globally inclusive. Clinical trial registration Not applicable.

research.abstract: Introduction TB incidence in Suriname has remained stable over the last decade. Understanding transmission patterns is essential for developing effective TB control strategies to interrupt ongoing transmission. Methods We conducted a descriptive analysis of routinely collected demographic and clinical data combined with whole-genome sequencing (WGS) data. Patients were classified into large (>6 patients) clusters, small (2-6 patients) clusters, or as non-clustered cases (unique). Bivariate and multivariable analyses compared patients in large clusters with those in small clusters and non-clustered patients. Epidemiological links obtained through patient interviews were compared with WGS findings. Results Of 698 TB patients notified during 2019-2024, WGS data were available for 368 (53%); 85% belonged to a genomic cluster. Indigenous ethnicity was inversely associated with membership in a large versus a small cluster (adjusted odds ratio [aOR] = 0.3; 95% confidence interval [CI] = 0.1-0.6). Compared with non-clustered cases, patients in large clusters were more likely to report illicit drug use (aOR = 3.0; 95% CI = 1.1-8.9). Conclusion WGS provided detailed insights into Mycobacterium tuberculosis transmission in Suriname. Illicit drug use was associated with membership in large transmission clusters, highlighting the need for early case finding and strengthened collaboration between TB and substance-use services.

research.abstract: ABSTRACT Background Circulating tumor DNA (ctDNA) is a promising biomarker for pediatric central nervous system (CNS) tumors, but limitations in sensitivity and universally accepted detection criteria remain. We evaluated multimodal ctDNA detection using a novel composite scoring framework integrating mutation, copy number, and fragmentomic analysis in longitudinal plasma and CSF samples from children with CNS tumors. Methods Tumor, blood and/or CSF samples were collected from pediatric CNS tumor patients. DNA was extracted from plasma, CSF, tumor, and whole blood. All samples underwent targeted and whole genome sequencing. Plasma and CSF samples were evaluated for ctDNA positivity—defined by a composite score ≥2—utilizing a tri-modal approach of whole genome sequencing for copy number alterations and fragmentomics and targeted sequencing. Results The cohort included 28 patients: medulloblastoma (39%), diffuse midline glioma (25%), high-grade glioma (18%), pilocytic astrocytoma (11%), and ependymoma (7%). A total of 140 plasma and 27 CSF samples were collected longitudinally. Combining all three modalities identified ctDNA in 70% of CSF and 17% of plasma samples, exceeding rates achieved by any single modality alone. Post-diagnosis plasma ctDNA positivity was significantly associated with worse progression-free and overall survival. CSF demonstrated significantly higher ctDNA signal intensity than plasma across all assay modalities. Conclusions A multimodal composite scoring approach improves longitudinal ctDNA detection in pediatric CNS tumors. Although CSF remains the most sensitive biofluid, plasma ctDNA reflects disease progression in select patients. These findings support integrated, multimodal liquid biopsy strategies for disease monitoring and highlight the need for prospective validation of standardized detection criteria. KEY POINTS Multimodal profiling of longitudinal plasma and CSF samples improves circulating tumor DNA detection in pediatric CNS tumors. Post-diagnosis plasma ctDNA positivity was associated with inferior progression-free survival despite the known challenges of plasma-based detection in pediatric CNS tumors. IMPORTANCE OF THE STUDY Pediatric brain tumors are among the most devastating childhood cancers, yet tools for non-invasive disease monitoring remain limited. Circulating tumor DNA (ctDNA) detected in blood and cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) offers a window into tumor biology without repeated surgery or biopsy. Here, we developed a multimodal scoring framework combining mutation analysis, copy number profiling, and DNA fragmentomics to standardize ctDNA detection across biofluids. Integrating all three methods improved detection beyond any single approach alone, and plasma ctDNA positivity was associated with significantly worse survival outcomes. These findings support the continued development of multimodal liquid biopsy as a clinical tool for disease monitoring in pediatric brain tumors.

research.abstract: A protein's sequence says what a gene could do in another species; the cells of that species say what it does there. Comparative genomics measures the first. Chimera measures the second, a gene's deployment, on the same genes and reports the difference. It aligns single-cell atlases across species in one generative model and returns, for every one-to-one ortholog, the evidence in the counts for a shared expression pattern, and {Delta}[a], the position of that evidence above or below what the protein's identity predicts. This difference is not sequence constraint under another name: across eight tissues, protein identity tracks dN/dS, whereas {Delta}[a] tracks neither. A gene therefore has two coordinates, not one, and the second can contradict the first: spermatocyte genes such as ZPBP2 keep their stage pattern on less conserved proteins, in eight held-out species, whereas conserved hepatocyte enzymes such as ALAS1 share their pattern but not their level. More broadly, genes of specialized cells sit above what their proteins predict in 23 of 24 cohorts, and approved drug targets do so more often than matched genes. Even among nearly identical proteins, where sequence can no longer tell genes apart, the count evidence still does. Nor does this rest on the model alone: independent data support the count evidence in liver and testis and, in a pre-specified test, {Delta}[a] in liver. With both coordinates, one can ask whether another species uses a gene as humans do, the premise of every animal model of a disease gene or drug target.

research.abstract: Abstract Ancestral sequences and substitution histories are usually averaged out in phylogenetic inference and are therefore not reported to the user. However, they can be recovered through ancestral sequence reconstruction (ASR) and stochastic character mapping. By implementing and validating a new ASR and stochastic mapping package compatible with both single-locus and multispecies coalescent analysis, we show how reconstructing substitution histories can enhance the information gained about the tempo and mode of molecular evolution. We observe that known substitution histories (simulated and empirical) are recovered more accurately and precisely on time trees compared with unconstrained and non-ultrametric substitution trees that lack temporal directionality (maximum likelihood and Bayesian). We show that codon-partition models with site-rate heterogeneity, based on the four nucleotide characters, can effectively approximate the histories of synonymous and non-synonymous change, while requiring far less runtime than computationally demanding codon models that require 61 characters. In turn, this provides low-bias estimation of dN/dS that is robust to non-stationarity in GC content, codon usage bias, and nucleotide exchangeability rates. Lastly, using three case studies, we demonstrate how the approach can recover expected patterns in molecular evolution and pathogen transmission: that i) smaller-bodied mammalian species tend to have faster synonymous substitution rates than larger relatives, ii) amino acid substitutions are correlated with 3Di structural changes in aminoacyl-tRNA synthetases, and iii) influenza A virus spread more frequently to nearby locations than distant ones, in a major H3N2 outbreak in New Zealand. These three trends were more pronounced when based on count estimates derived from stochastic mapping, relative to parametric rates and distances. Our open-source code comes with a user-friendly graphical interface, as the BeastMap package for BEAST 2; supporting a wide range of clock, site, and tree models and data types – including insertions and deletions – within a Bayesian phylogenetic framework.

research.abstract: Empyema necessitans is a rare complication of pleural infection in which infected pleural fluid extends through the parietal pleura into the surrounding soft tissues. We report the case of a 32-year-old man of Indian origin living in the United Kingdom who presented with worsening right-sided pleuritic chest pain, several months of night sweats, and a persistent dry cough. Five months earlier, he had been treated for right-sided pneumonia complicated by a pleural effusion, with persistent radiographic abnormalities on follow-up. Examination revealed reduced right-sided air entry and a tender, fluctuant swelling over the right posterior chest wall. Contrast-enhanced computed tomography demonstrated a posterior pleural collection extending through the chest wall into the adjacent paraspinal musculature, consistent with empyema necessitans. Ultrasound-guided aspiration yielded frank purulent fluid. Routine bacterial, anaerobic, and fungal cultures were negative. Acid-fast bacilli were not seen on initial microscopy; however, mycobacterial culture became positive after seven days, and polymerase chain reaction (PCR) testing of the pleural fluid detected Mycobacterium tuberculosis complex. Whole-genome sequencing subsequently identified a lineage 1 East-African-Indian-Ocean isolate with predicted susceptibility to first-line antituberculous agents. Four-drug antituberculous therapy was commenced, with subsequent clinical and radiological improvement. This case highlights chest wall swelling as an unusual presentation of tuberculosis and emphasizes the importance of cross-sectional imaging and targeted mycobacterial testing in establishing the diagnosis.

research.abstract: Polygonatum zanlanscianense Pamp. is a perennial herb (Asparagaceae) endemic to China, whose rhizomes are used in folk medicine as a substitute for Polygonati Rhizoma. Although its plastome has been reported, the mitogenome remained uncharacterized. Here, we assembled and annotated the complete linear mitogenome of P. zanlanscianense and analysed its gene repertoire, codon usage, repeats, RNA editing sites, MTPTs, synteny, phylogeny and Ka/Ks. The 689,491-bp mitogenome (GC 46.23%) encodes 56 genes: 36 PCGs, three rRNA genes and 17 tRNA genes. Codon usage is biased toward A/U-ending codons. We identified 68 SSRs, 25 tandem repeats, 1366 dispersed repeat pairs, 585 predicted C-to-U editing sites concentrated at the first and second codon positions, and 30 MTPT fragments accounting for 2.24% of the mitogenome. Phylogenetic analysis placed P. zanlanscianense as sister to Polygonatum kingianum Collett & Hemsl. Median Ka/Ks was below 1 for 33 of the 35 genes analysed; although rpl5 and ccmB showed elevated ratios, branch-site tests did not support positive selection. This first mitogenome of P. zanlanscianense provides genomic resources for comparative genomic, phylogenetic and medicinal studies in Polygonatum.

research.abstract: Background: Tuberculosis Diagnosis delays among tuberculosis patients can worsen infection transmission, disease severity, and mortality risk. Identifying factors influencing delays is crucial due to its persistence across healthcare levels and communities. The study identify determinants of tuberculosis diagnosis delay among patients attending public health facility of Metekel zone, Northwest Ethiopia:2023 Methods: An unmatched case-control study was conducted in Metekel zone health facilities from March to April 2023, involving 210 tuberculosis patients (103 cases, 107 controls) selected through systematic sampling. Data collected through structured questionnaires and STATA used for analysis, including bi-variable and multi-variable logistic regressions. Variables with p-value < 0.25 in bi-variable analysis were included in the final model after checking model fitness and multicollinearity. Results: Overall, 210 tuberculosis patients were included in the study. The following independent variables were associated diagnosis delay of tuberculosis: TB patients who travel greater than 10km (AOR: 2.941, (95 % CI: 1.509, 5.731); TB patients who are living at rural area (AOR: 4.135, 95 % CI :1.759, 9.723); TB patients who prior visit in holly-water and traditional medicine [AOR: 2.978, (95% CI: 1.292, 6.863); poor knowledge about TB [AOR: 2.826, (95% CI: 1.404, 5.687)]. Conclusion: Tuberculosis diagnosis delay is a major challenge to eliminate tuberculosis by breaking the chain of transmission. This study can be attributed to factors including place of residence being rural, poor knowledge about tuberculosis, non-health facility initial actions upon symptom onset, and far distance to health institutions. Recognizing these determinants helps in identifying and addressing barriers inhibiting early diagnosis, potentially improving healthcare access and promoting more timely diagnosis and treatment for tuberculosis patients.

research.abstract: Multidrug efflux pumps are major drivers of antimicrobial resistance, but overlapping resistance mechanisms mask the physiological limits of efflux alone. Bacterial genomes encode a large repertoire of multidrug efflux pumps, which could theoretically combine to achieve exceptionally high levels of resistance. To delineate the extent of resistance achievable through efflux driven adaptation, we performed adaptive laboratory evolution of Mycobacterium smegmatis mc²155 wild-type and efflux-deleted (ΔlfrA, ΔefpA) strains against ethidium bromide, a broad-spectrum efflux substrate. Despite prolonged selection, resistance reproducibly plateaued at 8-16 fold increase in MIC under the tested conditions. This plateau emerged through distinct evolutionary trajectories characterized by non-overlapping efflux pump sets: from overexpression of the well-characterized lfrA to upregulation of multiple uncharacterized pumps, all conferring cross-resistance. Genetic reconstruction of mutations in a transcriptional regulator and a membrane protein, together with overexpression of efflux pumps, recapitulated the resistance phenotypes of the evolved strains. Sustained pump overexpression depleted membrane potential and drove metabolic suppression, suggesting that energetic exhaustion may constrain further increase in efflux-mediated resistance. Similar constraints were observed in Mycobacterium tuberculosis, indicating that they may extend to other mycobacterial species. Efflux-metabolic integration thus affects resistance evolution, revealing therapeutic vulnerabilities to combat multidrug resistance.

research.abstract: Abstract Blood-based biomarkers are transforming Alzheimer’s disease (AD) detection, with plasma tau phosphorylated at threonine 217 (p-tau217) being a leading candidate. However, circulating p-tau217 originates from both central nervous system (CNS) and non-CNS sources, limiting specificity. Here, we benchmark the performance of next-generation p-tau217 biomarkers that are selective for p-tau217 from predominantly CNS origin versus the conventional non-selective p-tau217. Across neuropathologically-defined, Aβ- and tau-neuroimaging–characterized, and memory clinic cohorts, plasma brain-derived-p-tau217 (BD-p-tau217)–either alone or in ratio with brain-derived tau expressed as a percentage (BD-p-tau217%)–identified AD pathology and clinical AD with larger effect sizes, higher discriminative accuracies, and improved sensitivity and specificity, outperforming conventional alternatives. Furthermore, BD-p-tau217% and BD-p-tau217 demonstrated more robust prediction of future clinical progression up to two decades later. Importantly, diagnostic performance remained high in older adults with diabetes and cardiovascular disease, populations in which standard p-tau217 showed reduced specificity. The findings were independently replicated in a large multicenter cohort, demonstrating the robustness and generalizability of the observed improvements across clinical, imaging, and longitudinal outcomes. These results establish plasma BD-p-tau217% and BD-p-tau217 as biologically grounded and clinically robust biomarkers that advance early detection, diagnosis and prognosis of AD. One Sentence Summary Plasma brain-derived p-tau217 and its ratio over brain-derived tau improve the specificity of the leading blood-based Alzheimer’s disease biomarker p-tau217.

research.abstract: Microbial culture collections and synthetic microbial communities (SynComs) are essential experimental resources for investigating underlying mechanisms of plant-microbe interactions. However, such resources remain scarce for agriculturally relevant crops. Here, we address this gap by developing TriMic, a community resource to investigate plant-microbe interactions in wheat. We employed a host-mediated isolation approach to obtain a bacterial collection from wheat roots and characterized its taxonomic representation and functional potential through whole-genome sequencing. We further evaluated the community dynamics of a consortium derived from this collection across time and wheat genotypes to inform the selection of a simplified community. TriMic includes core and keystone taxa reported in previous wheat microbiomes studies. Moreover, genomic analysis revealed genetic potential for diverse genes associated with plant colonization, nutrient cycling, plant growth promotion, and biosynthetic gene clusters with taxa exhibiting metabolic patterns associated with both generalist and specialist strategies. The proposed 15-member SynCom reflects the taxonomic and functional relevance of the full collection. By integrating publicly accessible bacterial isolates, whole-genome sequences, and an ecologically informed SynCom, TriMic provides a foundation for translating ecological and genomic observations into testable hypotheses, advancing mechanistic investigations of microbial community assembly and plant-microbiome interactions.

research.abstract: Abstract Plateau aquatic environments expose fishes to chronic cold, hypoxia, ultraviolet radiation and low productivity, providing natural systems for studying genomic features associated with environmental adaptation. Whether related fishes inhabiting similar cold-water plateau environments exhibit comparable or divergent genomic responses remains unclear. We compared two plateau cypriniform fishes, Aspiorhynchus laticeps and Diptychus maculatus, within a 12-species phylogenomic framework, integrating orthogroup inference, gene-family turnover, coding-sequence divergence, chromosome-scale synteny and duplicated gene-pair divergence profiling. The strongest contrasts occurred in species-specific orthogroups and gene-family turnover. Aspiorhynchus laticeps had a larger set of apparent species-specific orthogroups, enriched mainly in oocyte and reproductive processes, and its expanded families and elevated-ω orthogroups were associated with immune, receptor-mediated and membrane-associated functions. By contrast, D. maculatus had fewer species-specific orthogroups enriched for neural and synaptic processes and a contraction-dominated gene-family profile involving host defence, mucosal immunity and chromatin-related processes. The focal contrast did not exceed empirical background variation, and expansion-related computational analysis of gene family evolution (CAFE) estimates were associated with assembly continuity and input-gene properties. These findings indicate that ecologically similar plateau fishes may exhibit different combinations of candidate genomic features, highlighting the joint influence of ecological adaptation and genome history.
