research.abstract: Small lytic phages of the ssRNA Leviviricetes and ssDNA Microviricetes achieve host lysis by expression of a single protein, designated as an Sgl protein. Four ssRNA Sgls have been shown to inhibit steps in peptidoglycan biosynthesis: three target MurJ, the Lipid II flippase, and one targets MurA, the committed step of the pathway. A fifth Sgl, the E protein of the canonical ssDNA microvirus {varphi}X174, inhibits MraY, which catalyzes the synthesis of the first lipid-linked intermediate. This inhibition requires SlyD, a cytoplasmic FKBP-type peptidyl-prolyl cis-trans isomerase. The Sgl of the Caulobacter ssRNA phage {varphi}Cb5 (Cebevirus halophobicum) has not been characterized. Here, we present physiological evidence that Sgl{varphi}Cb5 targets MraY. Moreover, we show that, despite the absence of detectable sequence similarity, Sgl{varphi}Cb5 shares several features with the {varphi}X174 E protein, including the distribution of hydrophobic and charged residues, a proposed N-out, C-in membrane topology, and retention of lytic activity in an Sgl{varphi}Cb5 -LacZ fusion. Furthermore, expression of the Caulobacter cytoplasmic FKBP-type peptidyl-prolyl cis-trans isomerase CC2799 enhances Sgl{varphi}Cb5 -mediated lysis in E. coli. These parallels between Sgl function in a DNA phage and an RNA phage either represent remarkably consonant convergent evolution or some evolutionary cross-over event for which there is currently no precedent.

research.abstract: Climatic variation across latitude shapes lineage diversification and niche evolution. We integrated multilocus and genome-wide SNPs, morphological characters, historical biogeography, and phylogenetic comparative analyses for 391 sampled individuals representing 21 recognised Rana species across the Palearctic. Time-calibrated total-evidence analyses resolved three major stem lineages originating in the Early Miocene, 22.00 Mya, followed by radiations across East Asia and the central Palearctic. Biogeographic reconstruction supported a northward expansion of the Rana amurensis lineage into Siberia, c. 7.67 Mya, coinciding with relatively warm Arctic conditions. Climate-latitude relationships were weak across Ranidae, but stronger and lineage-dependent in Eastern Palearctic Rana, particularly in relation to monsoon-related climatic variables. Across lineages, broad latitudinal ranges evolved independently in Eurasian Pelophylax ridibundus, R. amurensis, R. dybowskii, and R. temporaria (c. 30.00 Mya), with additional origins in Nearctic Lithobates catesbeianus and L. sylvaticus (c. 12.00 Mya). This homoplasy highlights the influence of climatic transitions on ranid diversification.

Quartet multispecies coalescent species-tree inference (*ASTRAL v5.7.8 vs. Native Rust runie-quartet-coalescent across 10,858,000 quartets) achieves exact 1.0000 quartet score parity, 100.0% unrecoded topological identity (RF = 0/122 splits), and a 15.2×–16.4× Native Rust speedup while ABBA-BABA tests resolve syntopic karst introgression (D = +0.4220, Z = 9.26). research.abstract: Background Tuberculosis (TB) remains a leading infectious cause of death, with drug-resistant TB (DR-TB) challenging disease control. Brazil has a high TB burden, and Rio Grande do Sul state reports persistently high incidence and drug-resistance rates. The drivers shaping the regional DR-TB burden remain poorly characterised. Methods We conducted genomic surveillance of confirmed DR-TB cases in Rio Grande do Sul, Brazil, from January 2023 to September 2024. Clinical isolates underwent genotypic (gDST) and phenotypic drug susceptibility testing (pDST) and whole-genome sequencing (WGS). We analyzed 33 newly sequenced genomes and 267 historical Mycobacterium tuberculosis genomes collected in 2011-2019 to characterize resistance, transmission, and spatiotemporal patterns and estimate the contributions of transmitted and acquired rifampicin resistance. Findings Molecular testing detected rifampicin resistance missed by pDST, including borderline rpoB mutations in 18.2% and emerging resistance-associated variants in 3% of the 33 analyzed isolates. Conversely, pDST detected baseline bedaquiline resistance missed by WGS in one newly diagnosed case. Among 300 genomes, 181 (60.3%) clustered into 32 genomic clusters at a 5-SNP threshold, including 12 with long-term circulation and several spanning prisons and communities. Sublineage frequencies remained stable over time, whereas we observed marked geographic structuring and localized clonal expansion. Among 178 rifampicin-resistant isolates, transmission accounted for an estimated 79.2-88.2% of resistance, corresponding to 11.8-20.8% of cases arising through de novo acquisition during treatment. Interpretation Our findings identify active transmission as the main driver of rifampicin-resistant TB in Rio Grande do Sul, with long-term transmission chains extending across both incarcerated and community settings. These results underscore the urgent need to strengthen timely TB case detection and resistance testing, enhance contact investigations, and implement targeted interventions aiming to interrupt persistent transmission chains.

research.abstract: Background: Tuberculosis remains a major public health challenge in Ghana, where GeneXpert MTB/RIF serves as a first–line diagnostic tool. However, uncertainties about this method persist regarding specimen quality and the clinical significance of indeterminate rifampicin susceptibility results. Methods: We conducted a retrospective cross–sectional study of samples from 3,977 presumptive TB patients tested either at HopeXchange Medical Center (Kumasi) or Keta Municipal Hospital between January 2020 and December 2024. Demographic data, sputum macroscopic appearance, and GeneXpert results were analyzed using descriptive statistics and Fisher’s exact test. Results: Overall Mycobacterium tuberculosis (MTb) test positivity was 11.6% (461/3977). Males accounted for 63.3% of positive results, with the highest percentage among those ages 30–40 years. Mucopurulent specimens yielded the highest positivity rate (25.4%), compared to 4.0% of salivary specimens. Blood–stained sputum specimens (n=44) showed a 15.9% positivity rate. Although confirmed rifampicin resistance was low (1.7%), 9.3% of all MTb positive samples yielded an indeterminate result. The rate of indeterminate results from samples collected at Kwadaso Municipal increased from 7.3% in 2021 to 28.6% in 2024. Conclusion: These findings validate Ghana National Tuberculosis Program (NTP) guidelines emphasizing the reliability of mucopurulent specimen collection, but challenges the routine rejection of blood–stained sputum. The rising trend of indeterminate rifampicin results requires further investigation of circulating rpoB mutation profiles and quality assurance measures. Patients with indeterminate results should be further assessed using drug susceptibility testing to rule out rifampicin resistance. The findings provide actionable evidence to refine diagnostic algorithms and improve TB care in Ghana.

items.summary: Background The concurrent infection of Tuberculosis (TB) and Human Immunodeficiency Virus (HIV) constitutes a significant clinical challenge and public health emergency throughout Sub-Saharan Africa. Although national healthcare systems provide complimentary diagnostic and treatment services, early-stage mortality rates among individuals with dual infections remain critically elevated. This…

research.abstract: Background The concurrent infection of Tuberculosis (TB) and Human Immunodeficiency Virus (HIV) constitutes a significant clinical challenge and public health emergency throughout Sub-Saharan Africa. Although national healthcare systems provide complimentary diagnostic and treatment services, early-stage mortality rates among individuals with dual infections remain critically elevated. This investigation seeks to determine independent clinical, immunological, behavioral, and geographic factors associated with mortality outcomes in TB/HIV co-infected populations within the Benoue Department of North Cameroon, employing district-level primary analytical modeling supplemented by secondary sensitivity analyses to mitigate potential bias from limited data availability. Methods A mixed retrospective and prospective cohort investigation was described, encompassing 406 co-infected individuals receiving treatment across all 14 Diagnostic and Treatment Centers (CDTs) distributed throughout the 8 health districts of the department during the period from January 1, 2022, through December 31, 2023, with extension of tuberculosis monitoring treatment ended on November 30, 2024. Statistical analysis conducted using SPSS version 25 incorporated preliminary bivariate Chi-square testing (p < 0.05) succeeded by primary multivariate binary logistic regression modeling and a supplementary sensitivity analysis stratifying geographic location into urban central versus combined peripheral and rural district categories [1-26]. Results Among 3,883 patients initiating tuberculosis treatment, 406 had concurrent HIV infection (10.46% prevalence). This co-infected group experienced significantly higher mortality at 15.02% (61/406), accounting for 84.72% (61/72) of all tuberculosis-related deaths in the department (p < 0.05). Multivariate analysis identified multiple independent mortality risk factors: geographic location in outlying districts (Gashiga: AOR = 56.81 [1.52-2127.84], p = 0.029; Garoua II: AOR = 48.36 [3.10-755.42], p = 0.006; Pitoa: AOR = 48.21 [2.53-918.98], p = 0.010; Lagdo: AOR = 28.63 [1.70-481.03], p = 0.020), severe immunosuppression at WHO Stage III (AOR = 9.88 [2.28-42.89], p = 0.002) and Stage IV (AOR = 10.81 [4.77-24.54], p < 0.001), inadequate medication adherence (AOR = 4.86 [1.14-20.69], p = 0.033), and elevated viral load (AOR = 7.46 [1.73-32.25], p = 0.007). A secondary sensitivity analysis that combined outlying district categories substantially decreased standard errors from 1.849 to 0.485 and generated a precise 95% confidence interval (AOR = 9.40 [3.63-24.32], p < 0.001), confirming that unequal healthcare access in rural areas represents a critical driver of excess mortality. Conclusion The heightened early mortality in TB/HIV co-infected individuals in North Cameroon stems from geographic variations in healthcare availability, late clinical diagnosis, poor medication compliance, and gaps in viral load monitoring systems. Reducing this mortality requires introducing rapid point-of-care viral load testing, establishing accessible molecular diagnostic facilities across regions, and deploying community-based programs to improve treatment compliance.

research.abstract: Computing phylogenetic likelihoods becomes challenging when the continuous-time Markov chain has a large state space. At each branch, pruning algorithms require terms of the form $e^{Q t}\cdot B$, where $Q$ is an $S \times S$ rate matrix (e.g., for $S$ states), $t$ is a branch length, and the columns of matrix $B$ (e.g., $B \in \mathbb{R}_{+}^{S \times L}$) are partial-likelihood vectors for $L$ site patterns. Many implementations calculate the dense transition matrix $P(t)=e^{Q t}$ via eigendecomposition and multiply it by $B$. This strategy is efficient for small state spaces, but it can be inefficient for large sparse rate matrices because forming $P(t)$ or its eigen vector matrices destroys sparsity and its cost may not be well amortized when $L$ is small. We implement an alternative likelihood kernel based on the Al-Mohy and Higham (2011) algorithm for computing the action of the matrix exponential directly, avoiding explicit construction of $P(t)$ or its eigen vector matrices. The resulting method takes full advantage of the sparsity of $Q$. We implement this method as a CPU-based extension to the BEAGLE library and evaluate it on two large-state molecular models: a Markov-modulated codon model of heterotachy with $M$ selective regimes and $61\cdot M$ possible states, and a codon-pair model of interlocus gene conversion between two paralogs with $61^2=3\,721$ possible states. Our results characterize when action-based likelihood computation improves performance over calculating $e^{Q t}$ directly. We show that this method enables fast, scalable inference for complex models, removing a key computational barrier to the study of evolution with large state space models.

research.abstract: Purpose Molecular diagnostic tests and sputum-based assays are common techniques for the initial evaluation of tuberculosis (TB). However, given their limitations in certain clinical contexts, efforts have been made to develop other diagnostic markers. This review evaluated the diagnostic accuracy of a three-gene host-response test (TB score) for the diagnosis of TB. Methods We performed systematic searches in seven databases until July 2026. We included observational studies evaluating the diagnostic accuracy of the TB score to diagnosis of TB across different clinical contexts. Risk of bias was assessed using QUADAS-2. Meta-analysis was performed using the logit function, and GRADE was employed to assess certainty of evidence (CoE). Results Twenty-eight studies were included. For distinguishing pulmonary TB from other respiratory diseases, the TB score showed a pooled sensitivity and specificity of 0.80 (95% CI: 0.73-0.84) and 0.72 (95% CI: 0.64-0.78), respectively, with an AUC of 0.82. When comparing pulmonary TB to healthy controls, sensitivity was 0.75 and specificity was 0.86, with an AUC of 0.87. Performance was lower for meningeal tuberculosis (sensitivity 0.58; specificity 0.67) and for distinguishing active from latent TB (sensitivity 0.73; specificity 0.76). Risk of bias was generally low. The CoE for most outcomes was very low. Conclusion The TB score shows moderate diagnostic accuracy for pulmonary TB, with pooled sensitivity below the WHO TPP minimum for a standalone triage test. High heterogeneity and very low CoE limit confidence in these findings. Its potential role as a complementary tool remains investigational and requires validation in prospective studies.

research.abstract: Abstract Background Understanding why species diversity is so unevenly distributed across the Tree of Life remains a central question in evolutionary biology. With more than 3,100 species, Astragalus (Fabaceae) is the largest genus of flowering plants and provides an exceptional system for investigating the factors of angiosperm megadiversity. However, despite recent phylogenomic advances, uncertainties in phylogenetic relationships and limited integration of available genomic resources have hindered comprehensive evolutionary analyses. Methods Here, we reconstruct the most comprehensive phylogenomic framework for Astragalus to date by integrating newly generated target enrichment data for 127 samples, representing 123 Astragalus taxa, with previously published target-capture, transcriptomic, and genome-skimming datasets. The resulting phylogeny includes 407 accessions representing 379 Astragalus species and provides a robust backbone for investigating diversification and genome evolution across the genus. Using a representative reduced dataset, we estimated divergence times, quantified diversification-rate heterogeneity, examined phylogenomic conflict, and evaluated evidence for whole-genome duplication (WGD). Key Results Our analyses recover a largely stable backbone for the deeper Astragalus lineages while revealing extensive gene-tree discordance concentrated in younger radiations, consistent with incomplete lineage sorting and reticulate evolution during rapid Miocene diversification. Diversification analyses indicate sustained lineage accumulation over approximately 18 million years, with pronounced rate shifts in several clades, particularly within the species-rich Neo-Astragalus lineage. Comparisons of alternative WGD scenarios across the phylogeny provided strongest support for a WGD at the crown node of Neo-Astragalus, with alternative placements receiving weaker support. This result provides a testable hypothesis for a WGD near the origin of the most rapidly diversifying lineage in the genus, although chromosome-scale genomic data will be required to confirm its occurrence and timing. Conclusions Together, our results indicate that the extraordinary diversity of Astragalus did not arise from a single evolutionary innovation or explosive radiation. Instead, megadiversity arose through the long-term interplay of sustained diversification, reticulate evolution, genome restructuring, and likely environmental change coupled with ecological adaptation. Beyond providing the most comprehensive phylogenomic hypothesis for the genus, this study establishes a robust framework for future investigations of biogeography, trait evolution, genome evolution, and the processes underlying exceptional species richness in flowering plants.

Consequently, applying the Genome Analysis…

research.abstract: Abstract Trait discovery in crops require reliable marker datasets, yet variant discovery remains constrained by the lack of standardised, high-confidence reference resources. Publicly available plant genomic resources often rely on outdated reference genomes, heterogenous pipelines, and generic variant hard-filtering thresholds derived from human studies. Consequently, applying the Genome Analysis Toolkit (GATK) Best Practices framework, particularly machine learning-based variant quality score recalibration (VQSR), remains challenging in crops lacking suitable training resources. Here, we present an unsupervised approach for variant quality assessment and generating cohort-specific training resources, enabling integration of VQSR into established GATK workflows without predefined high-confidence training variant sets. Using Brassica napus as a model, we use the Illumina 60k Brassica SNP array to establish a reference-specific truth set for base quality score recalibration (BQSR) and independent benchmarking. Gaussian mixture model (GMM)-based clustering of multidimensional variant annotation profiles identifies high-, intermediate-, and low-quality variant classes, which provide flexible training resources without requiring labelled training data. We further validate the approach in diploid Brassica oleracea and hexaploid wheat ( Triticum aestivum ), representing contrasting population characteristics and genome architectures. Across all three species, GMM-based clustering consistently identifies informative quality classes and enables cohort-specific recalibration of both SNPs and insertion-deletions (INDELs). Comparison with conventional hard filtering reveals discordant pass/fail classifications for up to 46.4% of SNPs and 37.8% of INDELs across evaluated cohorts, demonstrating that the approaches capture distinct aspects of variant quality. Our results establish unsupervised variant classification as transferable strategy for generating cohort-specific VQSR resources, extending established GATK workflows to crops lacking comprehensive genomic resources.

research.abstract: Physical activity levels are increasingly investigated as candidate digital biomarkers across a range of psychiatric and neurological disorders. Physical activity is heritable, with associated genetic variants implicating genes expressed in the central nervous system. However, its shared genetic architecture with disorders such as schizophrenia and Parkinson's disease (PD) remains poorly understood. Here, we applied complementary genome-wide methods to investigate the genetic overlap between physical activity and these disorders. We used a genome-wide association study (GWAS) of objectively measured physical activity (n = 89,683), enhanced through multi-trait GWAS incorporating self-reported activity measures (n = 124,842-377,234). In cross-trait analysis with recent GWAS of schizophrenia (n = 53,386 cases, 77,258 controls) and PD (63,555 cases, 17,700 proxy cases, and 1,746,386 controls), we find that while genetic correlations are negligible (rg=-0.02-0.02, p>0.05), polygenic overlap was substantial, with the majority of trait-influencing variants shared between the three traits. This contrast reflects mixed effect directions, which we show through convergent results from causal mixture modelling, local genetic correlations, and conjunctional false discovery rate analysis. Genes shared between activity and schizophrenia were differentially expressed in the amygdala and several basal ganglia structures, and associated with a range of cognitive-affective traits. In contrast, genes shared between activity and PD were largely associated with neurodegenerative disorders and structural brain phenotypes. Together, these findings suggest that activity draws on genes involved in motor, cognitive, affective and neurodegenerative processes, providing a genetic basis for its alteration across diverse neuropsychiatric disorders.

research.abstract: Streptococcus pyogenes causes diseases ranging from mild pharyngitis to life-threatening invasive infection, yet the genomic determinants of this variation remain poorly understood. We analyzed 1,863 publicly available genomes, whose pangenome comprises 6,568 genes (1,392 core and soft-core, 656 shell, and 4,520 cloud), and grouped isolates into 15 genetic groups with FastBAPS. Ten groups were monophyletic on the global phylogeny, and non-monophyly of the remaining five largely reflected the placement of isolates from group 12, which is dispersed across the tree. A GenomegaMap scan identified 163 of 3,147 genes with ω₀ > 1. These genes were depleted among core genes and enriched among cloud genes, a pattern consistent with positive selection on recently acquired genes but also with the retention of slightly deleterious variation in young genes. A putative IS transposase (K07497) was the most consistent functional enrichment signal, which led us to analyze insertion sequence (IS) elements directly. In group 12, complete IS copies within genomes were more often near-identical than in other groups (OR = 1.46), consistent with more recent IS activity, and genes with ω₀ > 1 were 2.9 times more likely than other accessory genes to lie within 5 kb of an IS element (8.8% vs. 3.0%; permutation p = 0.0006) after excluding IS-encoded genes. We did not detect this association in any other group, and most genes under selection were not IS-proximal.

research.abstract: Abstract Lysine-specific demethylase 1 (LSD1/KDM1A) demethylates both histone and non-histone substrates, recruits repressive chromatin complexes, and is increased in cancers. De novo LSD1 mutations impairing protein function lead to a rare developmental disorder, but the molecular details of the pathology remains unclear. Using patient-derived fibroblasts, reprogrammed pluripotent stem cells, and differentiated cells, we found over 4000 differentially expressed genes and 68 transcription factors (TFs) whose motif accessibilities changed upon LSD1 mutation. An enhancer-mediated gene regulatory network approach identified transcriptional repressors with impaired activity in fibroblast and stem cells, leading to erroneous activation of their target genes. We also revealed overall decreases in TF target gene expression during early lineage differentiation of LSD1 mutant stem cells, likely caused by increased activity of repressive histone deacetylases (HDACs), co-factors of LSD1. Indeed, an HDACs inhibitor restored changes in gene expression including downregulation phenotype. Our findings characterize the molecular pathogenesis of LSD1 mutations and suggest potential therapeutic strategies for the developmental disorder and cancers caused by LSD1 dysregulations.

items.summary: Glutamate links cellular metabolism with excitatory neurotransmission, yet the evolutionary histories of its metabolic enzymes, transporters, and receptor paralogues have not been compared within a common human-reference-anchored phylogenomic framework. research.abstract: Abstract Glutamate links cellular metabolism with excitatory neurotransmission, yet the evolutionary histories of its metabolic enzymes, transporters, and receptor paralogues have not been compared within a common human-reference-anchored phylogenomic framework. Here, we traced human UniProt/Swiss-Prot-associated protein lineages across 89 eukaryotic proteomes using homology searches, sequence and domain filtering, maximum-likelihood phylogenies assessed with transfer bootstrap expectation (TBE) and ultrafast bootstrap (UFBoot), sequence-stability analyses, and GeneRax gene-tree/species-tree reconciliation under a duplication–loss model. Metabolic enzyme homologues showed the broadest distributions: GLUD, GOT, and GPT were recovered across multiple eukaryotic supergroups, whereas GLS-associated sequences were detected in metazoans and the ichthyosporean Capsaspora owczarzaki . SLC17 and SLC1 transporter homologues were recovered only from sampled metazoans. Receptor distributions varied among families: GRM and GRIN sequences were detected across sampled cnidarians and bilaterians, GRIA and GRIK across bilaterian groups, and GRID only in seven sampled vertebrate species. Reconciliation mapped numerous paralogue-associated duplications to early vertebrate, gnathostome, and osteichthyan ancestral nodes, alongside independent lineage-specific expansions. Although many local phylogenetic relationships were supported, deeper relationships in some transporter and receptor families remained uncertain, with TBE and UFBoot providing different support values. These findings characterize the human-associated glutamatergic repertoire as an evolutionary mosaic of gene families with distinct taxonomic distributions and duplication histories. Because homology searches were anchored on human reference proteins, the inferred distributions represent detectable lineages in the sampled dataset rather than definitive evidence of gene-family origins or absence.
